title.zh: 卷一百三十 列傳第十七: 徹里 不忽木 完澤 阿魯渾薩理
title.en: Volume 130 Biographies 17: Cheli, Buhumu, Wanze, Aluhunsali
title.raw: 卷一百三十 列傳第十七: 徹里 不忽木 完澤 阿魯渾薩理 Volume 130 Biographies 17: Cheli, Buhumu, Wanze, Aluhunsali

sentences.zh: 元史 卷一百三十 列传第十七

translations.literal: History of Yuan, Volume 130, Biographies 17
translations.idiomatic: History of Yuan, Volume 130, Biography 17

sentences.zh: ○彻里

translations.literal: ○ Cheli
translations.idiomatic: Cheli

sentences.zh: 彻里，燕只吉台氏。

translations.literal: Cheli was of the Yanzhijitai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheli belonged to the Yanzhijitai clan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖太赤，为马步军都元帅，从太祖定中原，以功封徐、邳二州，因家于徐。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Taichi served as Commander-in-Chief of the Horse and Foot Armies; he followed the Taizu in pacifying the Central Plains and, for his merit, was enfeoffed with the two prefectures of Xu and Pi, and the family then settled in Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Taichi had been commander-in-chief of horse and foot. He followed Taizu in the conquest of the Central Plain and, rewarded for his service, was granted Xu and Pi prefectures, where the family made its home.

sentences.zh: 彻里幼孤，母蒲察氏教以读书。

translations.literal: Cheli was orphaned in childhood; his mother, of the Pucha clan, taught him to read.
translations.idiomatic: Cheli lost his father in childhood. His mother, a Pucha, taught him to read.

sentences.zh: 至元十八年，世祖召见，应对详雅，悦之，俾常侍左右，民间事时有所咨访。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan, Shizu summoned him; his replies were thorough and refined, and the emperor was pleased, making him attend constantly at his side and sometimes consulting him on matters among the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of the Zhiyuan era (1281), Kublai summoned him. Cheli answered with polish and ease, and the emperor was pleased. He kept Cheli constantly at his side and would consult him from time to time on conditions among the people.

sentences.zh: 从征东北边还，因言大军所过，民不胜烦扰，寒饿且死，宜加赈给，帝从之，乃赐边民谷帛牛马有差，赖以存活者众。

translations.literal: Returning from campaigning on the northeastern frontier, he said that wherever the great army had passed the people could not bear the harassment and were dying from cold and hunger; relief should be increased. The emperor agreed, and grain, cloth, cattle, and horses were given to the border people in varying amounts; many survived thereby.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from a campaign on the northeastern frontier, he reported that wherever the main army had marched, the populace had been harried beyond endurance and many were perishing from cold and hunger. Relief should be sent, he urged. The emperor agreed, and grain, cloth, cattle, and horses were distributed to the border people in proportion to their need. Many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 擢利用监。

translations.literal: He was promoted to the Directorate of Utilization.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the Directorate of Utilization.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，奉使江南，省风俗，访遗逸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was sent on mission to Jiangnan to inspect local customs and seek out recluses and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1286), he was dispatched to Jiangnan to survey local customs and seek out recluses and men of talent.

sentences.zh: 时行省理财方急，卖所在学田以价输官。

translations.literal: At that time the provincial administration was urgently raising funds and was selling local school lands and remitting the proceeds to the government.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial administration was then urgently raising revenue and was selling school lands throughout the region, forwarding the proceeds to the court.

sentences.zh: 彻里曰：「学田所以供祭礼、育人才也，安可鬻？」

translations.literal: Cheli said, "School lands exist to supply sacrificial rites and nurture talent. How can they be sold?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheli said, "School lands exist to fund sacrifices and nurture talent. How can they be sold off?"

sentences.zh: 遽止之。

translations.literal: He immediately halted it.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped the sale at once.

sentences.zh: 还朝以闻，帝嘉纳焉。

translations.literal: On returning to court he reported this, and the emperor commended and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to court he reported what he had done, and the emperor praised and approved it.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，分中书为尚书省。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Central Secretariat was split and a Ministry Secretariat was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (1287), the Central Secretariat was divided and a Ministry Secretariat was set up.

sentences.zh: 桑哥为相，引用党与，钩考天下钱粮，凡昔权臣阿合马积年负逋，举以中书失征奏，诛二参政。

translations.literal: Sangge became chief minister, brought in his faction, and audited the empire's revenue and grain accounts; all arrears accumulated over the years under the former powerful minister Ahmad were charged as failures of collection by the Central Secretariat, and two vice grand councilors were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge became chief minister, installed his faction, and launched a sweeping audit of revenue and grain accounts empire-wide. Arrears that had piled up for years under the former powerful minister Ahmad were blamed on the Central Secretariat for lax collection; two vice grand councilors were put to death.

sentences.zh: 行省乘风，督责尤峻。

translations.literal: The provincial administrations seized the moment and pressed collection with especial severity.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial administrations seized the moment and pressed collection with especial harshness.

sentences.zh: 主无所偿，则责及亲戚，或逮系邻党，械禁榜掠。

translations.literal: When the principal debtor could not pay, responsibility fell on kin; sometimes neighbors and associates were seized, shackled, imprisoned, and flogged.
translations.idiomatic: When the debtor could not pay, kin were held liable; neighbors and associates were sometimes seized, shackled, imprisoned, and beaten.

sentences.zh: 民不胜其苦，自裁及死狱者以百数，中外骚动。

translations.literal: The people could not bear the suffering; those who took their own lives or died in prison numbered in the hundreds, and disturbance spread within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: The people could not endure the suffering. Suicides and deaths in custody ran into the hundreds, and unrest spread through the court and the provinces alike.

sentences.zh: 廷臣顾忌，皆莫敢言。

translations.literal: Court officials were fearful and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials were afraid and none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 彻里乃于帝前具陈桑哥奸贪误国害民状，辞语激烈。

translations.literal: Cheli then set forth before the emperor in full detail Sangge's treachery, greed, harm to the state, and injury to the people, his words fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Cheli then laid out before the emperor in full Sangge's treachery, greed, and the harm he had done to state and people, speaking with fierce urgency.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，谓其毁诋大臣，失礼体，命左右批其颊。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, saying that he was slandering a high minister and violating propriety, and ordered those beside him to strike his cheeks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, saying Cheli was slandering a senior minister and had overstepped propriety, and ordered attendants to slap his face.

sentences.zh: 彻里辩愈力，且曰：「臣与桑哥无仇，所以力数其罪而不顾身者，正为国家计耳。

translations.literal: Cheli argued all the more forcefully and said, "Your servant bears no grudge against Sangge; the reason I enumerate his crimes with such force and without regard for my person is solely for the sake of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Cheli argued all the more forcefully. "I bear Sangge no personal grudge," he said. "I enumerate his crimes at the risk of my life solely for the sake of the realm.

sentences.zh: 苟畏圣怒而不复言，则奸臣何由而除，民害何由而息！

translations.literal: If I fear Your Majesty's wrath and speak no more, how will treacherous ministers be removed and the people's suffering be ended!
translations.idiomatic: If I fear Your Majesty's wrath and fall silent, how will treacherous ministers be removed and the people's suffering be ended!

sentences.zh: 且使陛下有拒谏之名，臣窃惧焉。」

translations.literal: Moreover, it would give Your Majesty the name of rejecting remonstrance — your servant privately fears this."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, it would give Your Majesty a name for rejecting honest counsel — that is what I fear."

sentences.zh: 于是帝大悟，即命帅羽林三百人往籍其家，得珍宝如内藏之半。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor came to a great awakening and immediately ordered three hundred guards of the Imperial Guard to go and inventory Sangge's household; the treasures seized amounted to half the imperial storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: At this the emperor saw clearly. He immediately sent three hundred guards of the Imperial Guard to inventory Sangge's household. The treasures seized amounted to half the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 桑哥既诛，诸枉系者始得释。

translations.literal: After Sangge was executed, all who had been wrongly imprisoned were at last released.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sangge had been executed, all who had been wrongly imprisoned were at last released.

sentences.zh: 复奉旨往江南，籍桑哥姻党江浙省臣乌马兒、蔑列、忻都、王济，湖广省臣要束木等，皆弃市，天下大快之。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to go to Jiangnan and inventory the property of Sangge's kin and faction: the Jiang-Zhe provincial ministers Umar, Mielie, Xindu, and Wang Ji, and the Huguang minister Yaosumu, among others — all were executed in the marketplace, and the empire rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to Jiangnan to seize the property of Sangge's kin and allies: the Jiang-Zhe provincial ministers Umar, Mielie, Xindu, and Wang Ji, and the Huguang minister Yaosumu, among others. All were executed in the marketplace, and the empire rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 彻里往来，凡四道徐，皆过门不入。

translations.literal: In all his comings and goings Cheli passed through Xu four times and each time went past his gate without entering.
translations.idiomatic: On all his journeys Cheli passed through Xu four times and each time went past his own gate without entering.

sentences.zh: 进拜御史中丞，俄升福建行省平章政事，赐黄金五十两、白金五千两。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Censor-in-Chief and soon promoted to Pacification Commissioner of Fujian Province, and was granted fifty taels of gold and five thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and soon made pacification commissioner of Fujian Province, with a grant of fifty taels of gold and five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 汀、漳剧盗欧狗久不平，遂引兵征之，号令严肃，所过秋毫无犯。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Ougou in Ting and Zhang had long been unrestful; he therefore led troops to campaign against him, his orders strict and disciplined, and wherever they passed not the slightest harm was done.
translations.idiomatic: The fierce bandit Ougou in Ting and Zhang had long defied pacification. Cheli led troops against him. His orders were strict and discipline firm; wherever the army passed, not a stalk of grain was touched.

sentences.zh: 有降者，则劳以酒食而慰遣之，曰：「吾意汝岂反者耶，良由官吏污暴所致。

translations.literal: When there were those who surrendered, he would treat them with wine and food, comfort them, and send them away, saying, "I do not think you were truly rebels; this was surely brought on by the filth and violence of officials.
translations.idiomatic: When men surrendered, he feasted them with wine and food, comforted them, and sent them home, saying, "I do not believe you were rebels at heart. This was surely brought on by corrupt and brutal officials.

sentences.zh: 今既来归，即为平民，吾安忍罪汝。

translations.literal: Now that you have come back, you are simply common people — how could I bear to punish you?
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have come back, you are simply common people. How could I bear to punish you?

sentences.zh: 其返汝耕桑，安汝田里，毋恐。」

translations.literal: Go back to your farming and sericulture, settle your fields and hamlets, and have no fear."
translations.idiomatic: Go back to your fields and mulberry groves, settle your homes, and have no fear."

sentences.zh: 他栅闻之，悉款附。

translations.literal: When other stockades heard this, all submitted in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: When other stockades heard this, all submitted in good faith.

sentences.zh: 未几，欧狗为其党缚致于军，枭首以徇，胁从者不戮一人，汀、漳平。

translations.literal: Before long Ougou was bound by his own followers and delivered to the army; his head was displayed as a warning, and not one of those who had followed under coercion was killed — Ting and Zhang were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ougou's own followers bound him and delivered him to the army. His head was displayed as a warning, and not one coerced follower was put to death. Ting and Zhang were pacified.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，帝不豫，彻里驰还京师，侍医药。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year the emperor fell ill; Cheli galloped back to the capital and attended him with medicines.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year (1294) the emperor fell ill. Cheli galloped back to the capital and attended him with medicines.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，与诸王大臣共定策，迎立成宗。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, he joined the princes and great ministers in settling the succession and welcomed Chengzong to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, he joined the princes and senior ministers in settling the succession and welcomed Chengzong to the throne.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，拜江南诸道行台御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Regional Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Dade era (1297) he was appointed censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan regional censorate.

sentences.zh: 一日，召都事贾钧谓曰：「国家置御史臺，所以肃清庶官、美风俗、兴教化也。

translations.literal: One day he summoned the Secretariat Officer Jia Jun and said, "The state established the Censorate to purify the ranks of officials, refine custom, and promote moral transformation.
translations.idiomatic: One day he summoned his secretariat officer Jia Jun and said, "The state established the Censorate to keep officials honest, refine custom, and promote moral transformation.

sentences.zh: 乃者御史不存大体，按巡以苛为明，征赃以多为功，至有迫子证父、弟证兄、奴讦主者。

translations.literal: Yet lately censors have not kept the larger purpose in view: on inspection tours they take harshness for clarity, and in pursuing illicit gains they take quantity for merit — even to the point of forcing sons to testify against fathers, younger brothers against elder brothers, and slaves to accuse their masters.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately censors have lost sight of the larger purpose. On inspection tours they take harshness for clarity; in pursuing illicit gains they take quantity for merit — even forcing sons to testify against fathers, younger brothers against elders, and slaves to accuse their masters.

sentences.zh: 伤风败教，莫兹为甚。

translations.literal: Nothing does more harm to custom and moral teaching than this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing does more harm to custom and moral teaching than this.

sentences.zh: 君为我语诸御史，毋庸效尤为也。」

translations.literal: Please tell all the censors for me that they must not imitate such excess."
translations.idiomatic: Tell all the censors for me that they must not imitate such excess."

sentences.zh: 帝闻而善之，改江浙行省平章政事。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this he approved, and Cheli was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang-Zhe Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he approved, and Cheli was transferred to pacification commissioner of Jiang-Zhe Province.

sentences.zh: 江浙税粮甲天下，平江、嘉兴、湖州三郡当江浙什六七，而其地极下，水钟为震泽。

translations.literal: Jiang-Zhe's tax grain led the empire; the three prefectures of Pingjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou accounted for six or seven tenths of Jiang-Zhe, yet their land was extremely low-lying, and the waters gathered into Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Zhe's tax grain led the empire. Pingjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou together accounted for six or seven tenths of Jiang-Zhe's yield, yet their land was extremely low-lying and the waters gathered in Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 震泽之注，由吴松江入海。

translations.literal: The outflow of Lake Tai passed through the Wusong River to enter the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Lake Tai's outflow passed through the Wusong River to reach the sea.

sentences.zh: 岁久，江淤塞，豪民利之，封土为田，水道淤塞，由是浸淫泛溢，败诸郡禾稼。

translations.literal: Over the years the river silted up; powerful families profited by it, enclosing land as fields, and the waterways clogged; thereby the waters spread and overflowed, ruining the grain crops of the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years the river silted up. Powerful families profited by enclosing the land as fields, and the waterways clogged. The waters then spread and overflowed, ruining the grain crops of the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命行省疏导之，发卒数万人，彻里董其役，凡四阅月毕工。

translations.literal: The court ordered the province to dredge and clear it; tens of thousands of laborers were mobilized, and Cheli supervised the work; in all it was completed in four months.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the province to dredge and clear the waterways. Tens of thousands of laborers were mobilized, and Cheli supervised the work. The project was completed in four months.

sentences.zh: 九年，召入为中书平章政事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned to the capital as Pacification Commissioner of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1305) he was summoned to the capital as pacification commissioner of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十月，以疾薨，年四十七。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he died of illness, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he died of illness, aged forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 薨之日，家资不满二百缗，人服其廉。

translations.literal: On the day of his death his household possessions amounted to less than two hundred strings of cash; people admired his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his death his household possessions amounted to less than two hundred strings of cash. All admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 赠推忠守正佐理功臣、太傅、开府仪同三司、上柱国，追封徐国公，谥忠肃。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Upholds Rectitude, and Assists in Governance, Grand Tutor, Grand Master of the Palace with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, and Pillar of the State of the First Rank; enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Xu with the posthumous name Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Upholds Rectitude, and Assists in Governance, together with Grand Tutor, Grand Master of the Palace with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, and Pillar of the State of the First Rank. He was enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Xu with the posthumous name Zhongsu (Loyal and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 至治二年，加赠宣忠同德弼亮功臣、太师、开府仪同三司、上柱国，追封武宁王，谥正宪。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he was further granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Proclaims Loyalty, Shares Virtue, and Illuminates with Aid, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, and Pillar of the State of the First Rank; enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Wuning with the posthumous name Zhengxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizhi (1322) he was further granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Proclaims Loyalty, Shares Virtue, and Illuminates with Aid, together with Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, and Pillar of the State of the First Rank. He was enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Wuning with the posthumous name Zhengxian (Upright and Law-abiding).

sentences.zh: 子朵兒只，江浙行省左丞。

translations.literal: His son Duorezhi served as Left Vice Councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duorezhi served as left vice councilor of Jiang-Zhe Province.

sentences.zh: ○不忽木

translations.literal: ○ Buhumu
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu

sentences.zh: 不忽木，一名时用，字用臣，世为康里部大人。

translations.literal: Buhumu, also named Shiyong, style Yunchen, for generations a great man of the Kangli tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu, also called Shiyong, style Yunchen, came from a line of great men of the Kangli tribe.

sentences.zh: 康里，即汉高车国也。

translations.literal: Kangli is the Gaoche state of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangli were the Gaoche people of Han times.

sentences.zh: 祖海蓝伯，尝事克烈王可汗。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hailanbo had once served the Kerait Wang Khan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hailanbo had once served Wang Khan of the Kerait.

sentences.zh: 王可汗灭，即弃家从数千骑望西北驰去，太祖遣使招之，答曰：「昔与帝同事王可汗，今王可汗既亡，不忍改所事。」

translations.literal: When Wang Khan was destroyed, he abandoned his household and with several thousand horsemen galloped off toward the northwest. The Taizu sent envoys to summon him; he replied, "In former days I and Your Majesty both served Wang Khan; now that Wang Khan is gone, I cannot bear to change whom I serve."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Khan fell, he abandoned his household and rode northwest with several thousand horsemen. Taizu sent envoys to summon him. He replied, "Your Majesty and I once served Wang Khan together. Now that Wang Khan is gone, I cannot bear to change whom I serve."

sentences.zh: 遂去，莫知所之。

translations.literal: He then departed, and none knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: He then departed, and none knew where he went.

sentences.zh: 子十人，皆为太祖所虏，燕真最幼，年方六岁，太祖以赐庄圣皇后。

translations.literal: His ten sons were all captured by the Taizu; Yan Zhen was the youngest, only six years old, and the Taizu gave him to Empress Zhuang Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: His ten sons were all captured by Taizu. Yan Zhen was the youngest, only six years old, and Taizu gave him to Empress Zhuang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 后怜而育之，遣侍世祖于籓邸。

translations.literal: The empress pitied and raised him, and sent him to attend Shizu at the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: The empress took pity on him and raised him, then sent him to attend Kublai at the princely residence.

sentences.zh: 长从征伐，有功。

translations.literal: When grown he followed on campaigns and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he followed on campaigns and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 世祖威名日盛，宪宗将伐宋，命以居守。

translations.literal: Shizu's renown grew daily; Möngke was about to campaign against Song and ordered him to remain and guard the residence.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai's renown grew daily. When Möngke prepared to campaign against Song, he ordered Kublai to remain behind and guard the residence.

sentences.zh: 燕真曰：「主上素有疑志，今乘舆远涉危难之地，殿下以皇弟独处安全，可乎？」

translations.literal: Yan Zhen said, "Our lord has long harbored suspicions; now the imperial carriage goes far into a land of peril and hardship, while Your Highness as imperial younger brother remains alone in safety — is this fitting?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen said, "The Great Khan has long been suspicious. Now he goes far into peril while Your Highness, his younger brother, remains alone in safety. Is that fitting?"

sentences.zh: 世祖然之，因请从南征。

translations.literal: Shizu agreed and therefore requested to join the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai saw he was right and asked to join the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 宪宗喜，即分兵命趋鄂州，而自将攻蜀之钓鱼山，令阿里不哥居守。

translations.literal: Möngke was pleased and immediately divided the army, ordering him to advance on Ezhou, while he himself led the attack on Diaoyu Mountain in Shu and ordered Ariq Böke to remain and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Möngke was pleased. He divided the army, ordering Kublai to advance on Ezhou while he himself led the attack on Diaoyu Mountain in Shu and left Ariq Böke to guard the rear.

sentences.zh: 宪宗崩，燕真统世祖留部，觉阿里不哥有异志，奉皇后稍引而南，与世祖会于上都。

translations.literal: When Möngke died, Yan Zhen commanded the forces Shizu had left behind; perceiving that Ariq Böke harbored divergent intentions, he escorted the empress and gradually withdrew south, joining Shizu at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke died, Yan Zhen commanded the forces Kublai had left behind. Seeing that Ariq Böke harbored divergent ambitions, he escorted the empress and gradually withdrew south, joining Kublai at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，燕真未及大用而卒，官止卫率。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Yan Zhen died before he could be greatly employed; his highest office was Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai took the throne, Yan Zhen died before he could be greatly employed. His highest office was commandant of the guard.

sentences.zh: 不忽木其仲子也，资禀英特，进止详雅，世祖奇之，命给事裕宗东宫，师事太子赞善王恂。

translations.literal: Buhumu was his second son; his endowment was outstanding, his bearing refined and elegant. Shizu marveled at him and ordered him to serve in the Eastern Palace of Crown Prince Yuzong, studying under the Crown Prince's Tutor Wang Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu was his second son. He was exceptionally gifted and carried himself with refined ease. Kublai took notice and assigned him to the Eastern Palace of Crown Prince Yuzong, where he studied under the crown prince's tutor Wang Xun.

sentences.zh: 恂从北征，乃受学于国子祭酒许衡。

translations.literal: When Xun went on the northern campaign, Buhumu then received instruction from the Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, Xu Heng.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xun went on the northern campaign, Buhumu studied under Xu Heng, chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 日记数千言，衡每称之，以为有公辅器。

translations.literal: Each day he wrote several thousand characters; Heng often praised him, considering that he had the makings of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he wrote several thousand characters. Xu Heng often praised him, saying he had the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 世祖尝欲观国子所书字，不忽木年十六，独书《贞观政要》数十事以进，帝知其寓规谏意，嘉叹久之。

translations.literal: Shizu once wished to see specimens of the students' calligraphy; Buhumu, aged sixteen, alone copied out several dozen passages from the Essentials of Government in the Zhenguan Reign and presented them; the emperor knew he intended admonition and remonstrance and praised him at length.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai once wished to see specimens of the students' calligraphy. Buhumu, aged sixteen, alone copied out several dozen passages from the Essentials of Government in the Zhenguan Reign and presented them. The emperor saw the admonitory intent and praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 衡纂历代帝王名谥、统系、岁年，为书授诸生，不忽木读数过即成诵，帝召试，不遗一字。

translations.literal: Heng compiled the posthumous names, titles, lines of descent, and reign years of emperors through the ages into a book for the students; Buhumu read it a few times and could recite it; the emperor summoned him for examination and he omitted not a single character.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Heng compiled the posthumous names, titles, lines of descent, and reign years of emperors through the ages into a book for the students. Buhumu read it a few times and could recite it entire. The emperor summoned him for examination and he omitted not a single character.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，与同舍生坚童、太答、秃鲁等上疏曰： 臣等闻之，《学记》曰：「君子如欲化民成俗，其必由学乎！」

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, together with his fellow students Jiantong, Taida, Tulü, and others he submitted a memorial saying: We have heard that the Record of Learning says, "If the gentleman wishes to transform the people and perfect custom, must he not do so through learning?"
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan (1276), together with his fellow students Jiantong, Taida, Tulü, and others he submitted a memorial: We have heard that the Record of Learning says, "If the gentleman wishes to transform the people and perfect custom, must he not do so through learning?"

sentences.zh: 「玉不琢不成器，人不学不知道。」

translations.literal: "Jade unworked does not become a vessel; a person who does not study does not know the Way."
translations.idiomatic: "Jade unworked does not become a vessel; a person who does not study does not know the Way."

sentences.zh: 故古之王者，建国君民，教学为先。

translations.literal: Therefore the kings of antiquity, in founding the state and ruling the people, put instruction first.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the kings of antiquity, in founding the state and ruling the people, put instruction first.

sentences.zh: 盖自尧、舜、禹、汤、文、武之世，莫不有学，故其治隆于上，俗美于下，而为后世所法。

translations.literal: From the age of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, none lacked schools; therefore their governance flourished above and custom was refined below, and they became models for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, none lacked schools. Their governance flourished above and custom was refined below, and they became models for later ages.

sentences.zh: 降至汉朝，亦建学校，诏诸生课试补官。

translations.literal: Down to the Han dynasty, schools were also established, and an edict ordered students examined by course and appointed to office according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Han dynasty, schools were also established, and students were examined and appointed to office according to merit.

sentences.zh: 魏道武帝起自北方，既定中原，增置生员三千，儒学以兴。

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu of Wei rose from the north; after he had settled the Central Plains he added three thousand students, and Confucian learning flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu of Wei rose from the north. After he settled the Central Plain he added three thousand students, and Confucian learning flourished.

sentences.zh: 此历代皆有学校之证也。

translations.literal: This is proof that every dynasty had schools.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that every dynasty had maintained schools.

sentences.zh: 臣等今复取平南之君建置学校者，为陛下陈之。

translations.literal: We now take again the rulers who pacified the south and established schools, and set them forth for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: We now cite for Your Majesty the rulers who pacified the south and established schools.

sentences.zh: 晋武帝尝平吴矣，始起国子学。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin had pacified Wu and then first established the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Jin had pacified Wu, he first established the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝尝灭陈矣，俾国子寺不隶太常。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui had destroyed Chen and made the Directorate of the Imperial Academy independent of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Sui had destroyed Chen, he made the Directorate of the Imperial Academy independent of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 唐高祖尝灭梁矣，诏诸州县及乡并令置学。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Tang had destroyed Liang and ordered that schools be established in all prefectures, counties, and townships.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozu of Tang had destroyed Liang, he ordered schools established in all prefectures, counties, and townships.

sentences.zh: 及至太宗，数幸国学，增筑学舍至千二百间，国学、太学、四门学亦增生员，其书、算各置博士，乃至高丽、百济、新罗、高昌、吐蕃诸国酋长亦遣子弟入学，国学之内至八千餘人。

translations.literal: When it came to Taizong, he often visited the Imperial Academy, increased the school buildings to twelve hundred rooms, and also increased students in the Imperial Academy, the National University, and the Four Gates Academy; for the schools of writing and calculation he each appointed erudites; even the chieftains of Goryeo, Baekje, Silla, Gaochang, and Tibet sent their sons to study — within the Imperial Academy there came to be more than eight thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong he often visited the Imperial Academy, expanded the school buildings to twelve hundred rooms, and increased enrollment in the Imperial Academy, the National University, and the Four Gates Academy. He appointed erudites for the schools of writing and calculation. Even chieftains of Goryeo, Baekje, Silla, Gaochang, and Tibet sent their sons to study. The Imperial Academy came to hold more than eight thousand students.

sentences.zh: 高宗因之，遂令国子监领六学：一曰国子学，二曰太学，三曰四门学，四曰律学，五曰书学，六曰算学，各置生徒有差，皆承高祖之意也。

translations.literal: Gaozong followed this and ordered the Directorate of the Imperial Academy to oversee six schools: first the Imperial Academy, second the National University, third the Four Gates Academy, fourth the School of Law, fifth the School of Writing, sixth the School of Calculation — each with students in fixed numbers, all continuing Gaozu's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong followed this and ordered the Directorate of the Imperial Academy to oversee six schools: the Imperial Academy, the National University, the Four Gates Academy, the School of Law, the School of Writing, and the School of Calculation, each with a fixed number of students — all continuing Gaozu's intent.

sentences.zh: 然晋之平吴得户五十二万而已，隋之灭陈得郡县五百而已，唐之灭梁得户六十餘万而已，而其崇重学校已如此。

translations.literal: Yet Jin in pacifying Wu gained only five hundred twenty thousand households; Sui in destroying Chen gained only five hundred prefectures and counties; Tang in destroying Liang gained only a little more than six hundred thousand households — and yet they honored schools to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jin in pacifying Wu gained only five hundred twenty thousand households; Sui in destroying Chen gained only five hundred prefectures and counties; Tang in destroying Liang gained only a little more than six hundred thousand households — and still they honored schools to this degree.

sentences.zh: 况我堂堂大国，奄有江岭之地，计亡宋之户不下千万，此陛下神功，自古未有，而非晋、隋、唐之所敢比也。

translations.literal: How much more our great and august state, which holds the lands south of the Yangtze — the households of the fallen Song are estimated at no fewer than ten million; this is Your Majesty's divine achievement, unmatched since antiquity, and not to be compared with Jin, Sui, or Tang.
translations.idiomatic: How much more so for our great and august state, which holds the lands south of the Yangtze. The households of the fallen Song are estimated at no fewer than ten million. This is Your Majesty's divine achievement, unmatched since antiquity — not to be compared with Jin, Sui, or Tang.

sentences.zh: 然学校之政，尚未全举，臣窃惜之。

translations.literal: Yet the policy on schools has not been fully carried out — your servants privately regret this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the policy on schools has not been fully carried out. We regret this deeply.

sentences.zh: 臣等向被圣恩，俾习儒学。

translations.literal: We have been favored by the sage grace and ordered to study Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: We have been favored by Your Majesty's grace and ordered to study Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 钦惟圣意，岂不以诸色人仕宦者常多，蒙古人仕宦者尚少，而欲臣等晓识世务，以任陛下之使令乎？

translations.literal: Reverently considering the sage intent — is it not because people of various categories in office are often many while Mongols in office are still few, and Your Majesty wishes us to understand affairs of the age so as to bear Your Majesty's commissions?
translations.idiomatic: Reverently considering Your Majesty's intent — is it not because people of various categories already fill office while Mongols in office are still few, and you wish us to understand affairs of state so we may serve your commissions?

sentences.zh: 然以学制未定，朋从数少。

translations.literal: Yet because the school system is not yet settled and companions are few in number —
translations.idiomatic: Yet because the school system is not yet settled and our companions are few —

sentences.zh: 譬犹责嘉禾于数苗，求良骥于数马，臣等恐其不易得也。

translations.literal: it is like demanding fine grain from a few seedlings or seeking fine steeds from a few horses — your servants fear they will not easily be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: it is like demanding fine grain from a few seedlings or fine steeds from a few horses — we fear they will not easily be found.

sentences.zh: 为今之计，如欲人材众多，通习汉法，必如古昔遍立学校然后可。

translations.literal: For the present plan, if you wish talent to be numerous and thoroughly versed in Han institutions, you must, as in antiquity, establish schools everywhere — only then will it suffice.
translations.idiomatic: For the present, if you wish talent to be numerous and thoroughly versed in Han institutions, you must, as in antiquity, establish schools everywhere — only then will it suffice.

sentences.zh: 若曰未暇，宜且于大都弘阐国学。

translations.literal: If you say there is not yet leisure, you should for the present expand and clarify the Imperial Academy at Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: If you say there is not yet leisure, you should for the present expand the Imperial Academy at Dadu.

sentences.zh: 择蒙古人年十五以下、十岁以上质美者百人，百官子弟与凡民俊秀者百人，俾廪给各有定制。

translations.literal: Select a hundred Mongols of fine quality between ten and fifteen years of age, and a hundred sons of officials and outstanding commoners, and grant them stipends each according to fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Select a hundred fine Mongol youths between ten and fifteen years of age, and a hundred sons of officials and outstanding commoners, and grant them stipends according to fixed regulations.

sentences.zh: 选德业充备足为师表者，充司业、博士、助教而教育之。

translations.literal: Choose those whose virtue and learning are complete and sufficient to serve as models, and appoint them as Vice Chancellors, Erudites, and Assistant Instructors to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: Choose men of complete virtue and learning sufficient to serve as models, and appoint them vice chancellors, erudites, and assistant instructors to teach them.

sentences.zh: 使其教必本于人伦，明乎物理，为之讲解经传，授以修身、齐家、治国、平天下之道。

translations.literal: Let their instruction be rooted in human relations, clear on the principles of things; expound the classics and commentaries for them and teach them the Way of cultivating the person, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Let instruction be rooted in human relations and clear on the principles of things. Expound the classics and commentaries for them and teach them the way of cultivating the person, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其下复立数科，如小学、律、书、算之类。

translations.literal: Below this establish several branches, such as elementary learning, law, writing, and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Below this establish several branches, such as elementary learning, law, writing, and calculation.

sentences.zh: 每科设置教授，各令以本业训导。

translations.literal: For each branch appoint instructors and have each teach and guide according to his specialty.
translations.idiomatic: For each branch appoint instructors and have each teach according to his specialty.

sentences.zh: 小学科则令读诵经书，教以应对进退事长之节；

translations.literal: For the elementary-learning branch, have them read and recite the classics and books, and teach them the proprieties of responding, advancing, retreating, and serving elders;
translations.idiomatic: For the elementary-learning branch, students should read and recite the classics and be taught the proprieties of conversation, deportment, and serving their elders.

sentences.zh: 律科则专令通晓吏事；

translations.literal: For the law branch, have them specialize in mastering clerical and administrative affairs;
translations.idiomatic: The law branch should focus on mastering administrative and clerical affairs.

sentences.zh: 书科则专令晓习字画；

translations.literal: For the writing branch, have them specialize in learning script and characters;
translations.idiomatic: The writing branch should focus on mastering script and characters.

sentences.zh: 算科则专令熟闲算数。

translations.literal: For the calculation branch, have them specialize in becoming thoroughly skilled in reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: The calculation branch should focus on becoming thoroughly skilled in arithmetic.

sentences.zh: 或一艺通然后改授，或一日之间更次为之。

translations.literal: Either once one art is mastered, then change instruction; or within a single day rotate through them in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Students may proceed to a new subject only after mastering one art, or rotate through subjects within a single day.

sentences.zh: 俾国子学官总领其事，常加点勘，务要俱通，仍以义理为主。

translations.literal: Have the officials of the Directorate of Education oversee it all, constantly inspect and verify, require mastery of all, and still take principles and right meaning as primary.
translations.idiomatic: The officials of the Directorate of Education should oversee the whole program, conduct regular inspections, require students to master every subject, and always treat moral principles as primary.

sentences.zh: 有餘力者听令学作文字。

translations.literal: Those with surplus strength may be permitted to learn composition.
translations.idiomatic: Those with spare capacity may be permitted to study literary composition.

sentences.zh: 日月岁时，随其利钝，各责所就功课，程其勤惰而赏罚之。

translations.literal: By month, day, season, and year, according to their aptitude or dullness, assign each his completed lessons, measure diligence and idleness, and reward and punish accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: By month, season, and year, according to each student's aptitude, assess the lessons completed, measure diligence and idleness, and mete out rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 勤者则升之上舍，惰者则降之下舍，待其改过则复升之。

translations.literal: The diligent are promoted to the upper dormitory; the idle are demoted to the lower dormitory, and after they reform they are promoted again.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent students are promoted to the upper dormitory; idle ones are demoted to the lower dormitory and restored only after they reform.

sentences.zh: 假日则听令学射，自非假日，无故不令出学。

translations.literal: On holidays they may be permitted to practice archery; apart from holidays, without cause they are not permitted to leave the academy.
translations.idiomatic: On holidays students may practice archery; except on holidays, they may not leave the academy without good cause.

sentences.zh: 数年以后，上舍生学业有成就者，乃听学官保举，蒙古人若何品级，诸色人若何仕进。

translations.literal: After several years, upper-dormitory students whose learning has achieved success may then be permitted to be recommended by academy officials — what rank for Mongols, what office and advancement for persons of all other categories.
translations.idiomatic: After several years, upper-dormitory students who have achieved success in their studies may be recommended by academy officials — specifying what rank Mongols should receive and what offices persons of other categories should enter.

sentences.zh: 其未成就者，且令依旧学习，俟其可以从政，然后岁听学官举其贤者、能者，使之依例入仕。

translations.literal: Those not yet achieving success, for the time being let them continue study as before; when they can take part in governance, then each year permit academy officials to recommend the worthy and capable, and have them enter office according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Those who have not yet succeeded should continue their studies. When they are ready to serve in government, academy officials may each year recommend the worthy and capable among them for office according to established precedent.

sentences.zh: 其终不可教者，三年听令出学。

translations.literal: Those ultimately unteachable, after three years may be permitted to leave the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Those who prove unteachable after three years may be dismissed from the academy.

sentences.zh: 凡学政因革、生员增减，若得不时奏闻，则学无弊政，而天下之材亦皆观感而兴起矣。

translations.literal: For all changes in school administration, increases and decreases of enrolled students — if these can be reported in timely fashion, then the schools will be free of corrupt administration, and talents throughout the realm will likewise be moved by example and rise up.
translations.idiomatic: If changes in school administration and enrollment can be reported promptly to the throne, corrupt practice in education will be prevented, and talented men throughout the realm will be inspired to come forward.

sentences.zh: 然后续立郡县之学，求以化民成俗，无不可者。

translations.literal: Then establish schools in the commanderies and districts in succession, seeking to transform the people and complete customs — nothing in this would be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Schools could then be established in the commanderies and districts in succession, transforming the people and completing local custom — nothing would be beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 臣等愚幼，见于书、闻于师者如此。

translations.literal: We, your servants, young and ignorant, have seen in books and heard from teachers only this much.
translations.idiomatic: We, your servants, young and ignorant as we are, have learned no more than what books and our teachers have taught us.

sentences.zh: 未敢必其可行，伏望圣慈下臣此章，令诸老先与左丞王赞善等，商议条奏施行，臣等不胜至愿。

translations.literal: We dare not be certain it can be implemented. We prostrate ourselves hoping in sacred compassion you will transmit this our memorial below, and order the venerable elders together with Left Chancellor Wang Zanshan and others to discuss it, itemize it in memorial, and put it into effect — we could not exceed this our utmost wish.
translations.idiomatic: We dare not insist that our proposal will surely work. We humbly beseech Your Majesty in your sacred compassion to receive this memorial and charge the senior ministers, together with Left Chancellor Wang Zanshan and others, to discuss it, submit detailed recommendations, and implement what is agreed — this is our deepest wish.

sentences.zh: 书奏，帝览之喜。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; the Emperor read it and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor read it and was pleased.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授利用少监。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate for Profit and Use.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, he was appointed vice director of the Directorate for Profit and Use.

sentences.zh: 十五年，出为燕南河北道提刑按察副使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he went out as Vice Intendant of the Commission for Punishments and Inspection of the Yan South and Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed vice intendant of the Commission for Punishments and Inspection for the Yan South and Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 帝遣通事脱虎脱护送西僧往作佛事，还过真定，箠驿吏几死，诉之按察使，不敢问。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent the interpreter Tuoheduo to escort a Western monk to perform Buddhist rites. Returning they passed through Zhending; he beat a courier-station clerk nearly to death. The clerk complained to the intendant, who dared not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dispatched the interpreter Tuoheduo to escort a Western monk to perform Buddhist rites. On their return through Zhending, Tuoheduo beat a courier-station clerk nearly to death. The clerk lodged a complaint with the intendant, who dared not investigate.

sentences.zh: 不忽木受其状，以僧下狱。

translations.literal: Buhumu received the complaint and imprisoned the monk.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu accepted the complaint and imprisoned the monk.

sentences.zh: 脱虎脱直欲出僧，辞气倔强，不忽木令去其冠庭下，责以不职。

translations.literal: Tuoheduo at once sought to release the monk; his words were stubborn and defiant. Buhumu had his cap removed in the court below and reprimanded him for neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoheduo immediately sought to free the monk, speaking in a stubborn and defiant tone. Buhumu had his cap removed in open court and rebuked him for dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 脱虎脱逃归以闻，帝曰：「不忽木素刚正，必尔辈犯法故也。」

translations.literal: Tuoheduo fled back and reported it. The Emperor said: "Buhumu has always been upright and firm; surely you people violated the law — that is why."
translations.idiomatic: Tuoheduo fled home and reported the matter. The Emperor said, "Buhumu has always been upright and firm; you must have broken the law — that is why."

sentences.zh: 继而燕南奏至，帝曰：「我固知之。」

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Yan South's memorial arrived; the Emperor said: "I knew it all along."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the report from Yan South arrived. The Emperor said, "I knew it all along."

sentences.zh: 十九年，升提刑按察使。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, he was promoted to Intendant of the Commission for Punishments and Inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, he was promoted to intendant of the Commission for Punishments and Inspection.

sentences.zh: 有讼净州守臣盗官物者，净州本隶河东，特命不忽木往按之，归报称旨，赐白金千两、钞五千贯。

translations.literal: There was a case accusing the Jingzhou prefect of stealing government goods. Jingzhou originally was subordinate to Hedong; the Emperor specially ordered Buhumu to go investigate. On his return his report accorded with the Emperor's wish; he was granted one thousand taels of white silver and five thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: When an official of Jingzhou was accused of stealing government property, the Emperor specially ordered Buhumu — though Jingzhou normally fell under Hedong — to investigate. His report on returning pleased the Emperor, who rewarded him with one thousand taels of silver and five thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，召参议中书省事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, he was summoned to participate in deliberations on the affairs of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, he was summoned to serve as a deliberative official of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 时榷茶转运使卢世荣阿附宣政使桑哥，言能用己，则国赋可十倍于旧。

translations.literal: At the time the Tea Monopoly Transport Commissioner Lu Shirong fawned upon and attached himself to the Commissioner of Political Affairs Sangge, saying that if he were employed, state revenues could be ten times what they had been.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the tea monopoly transport commissioner Lu Shirong had curried favor with the commissioner of political affairs Sangge, claiming that if put to use he could increase state revenue tenfold.

sentences.zh: 帝以问不忽木，对曰：「自昔聚敛之臣，如桑弘羊、宇文融之徒，操利术以惑时君，始者莫不谓之忠，及其罪稔恶著，国与民俱困，虽悔何及。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Buhumu. He replied: "Since ancient times revenue-grabbing ministers such as Sang Hongyang, Yuwen Rong, and their kind, wielding profit-craft to beguile the ruler of the age — at first none failed to call them loyal; but when their crimes ripened and wickedness showed, state and people alike were exhausted. Even to regret was too late.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Buhumu, who replied, "Revenue-grabbing ministers of old, men like Sang Hongyang and Yuwen Rong, used schemes of profit to beguile their rulers. At first all called them loyal servants; but when their crimes matured and their evil became plain, both state and people were ruined — and regret came too late.

sentences.zh: 臣愿陛下无纳其说。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty not accept his proposal."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty not to accept his proposal."

sentences.zh: 帝不听，以世荣为右丞，不忽木遂辞参议不拜。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen; he made Shirong Right Chancellor, and Buhumu thereupon declined the deliberative post and refused to accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not listen. He made Lu Shirong right chancellor, and Buhumu declined the deliberative post and refused to accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，世荣以罪被诛，帝曰：「朕殊愧卿。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Shirong was executed for his crimes. The Emperor said: "I am deeply ashamed before you."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, Lu Shirong was executed for his crimes. The Emperor said, "I am deeply ashamed before you."

sentences.zh: 擢吏部尚书。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu was promoted to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 时方籍没阿合马家，其奴张散札兒等罪当死，缪言阿合马家赀隐寄者多，如尽得之，可资国用。

translations.literal: At the time they were confiscating the Ahama household's property. His slave Zhang Sanzhar and others, their crime warranting death, falsely said that much of Ahama's wealth was secretly deposited elsewhere; if all were obtained, it could supply state use.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the government was confiscating the property of Ahama's household. Ahama's slave Zhang Sanzhar, who deserved death for his crimes, falsely claimed that much of the family's wealth had been hidden elsewhere and that recovering it all would replenish the treasury.

sentences.zh: 遂钩考捕系，连及无辜，京师骚动。

translations.literal: Thereupon they tracked, examined, arrested, and imprisoned; the innocent were implicated as well, and the capital was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Officials launched sweeping investigations and arrests, implicating innocent people as well and throwing the capital into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 帝颇疑之，命丞相安童集六部长贰官询问其事，不忽木曰：「是奴为阿合马心腹爪牙，死有餘罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor was somewhat suspicious and ordered Chancellor Antong to assemble the heads and deputies of the Six Ministries to inquire into the matter. Buhumu said: "That slave was Ahama's trusted henchman; death left his guilt more than satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew suspicious and ordered Chancellor Antong to convene the heads and deputies of the Six Ministries to examine the matter. Buhumu said, "That slave was Ahama's trusted henchman; he deserved death many times over.

sentences.zh: 为此言者，盖欲苟延岁月，徼幸不死尔。

translations.literal: In making this statement, he surely sought to drag out time and count on luck not to die.
translations.idiomatic: He said this only to drag out his days and hope by luck to escape death.

sentences.zh: 岂可复受其诳，嫁祸善良耶？

translations.literal: How could one again accept his deception and shift calamity onto the good and innocent?
translations.idiomatic: How can we accept his deceit again and shift calamity onto innocent people?

sentences.zh: 急诛此徒，则怨谤自息。」

translations.literal: Execute these fellows at once, and complaints and slander will cease of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Execute these men at once, and public resentment will die down of its own accord."

sentences.zh: 丞相以其言入奏，帝悟，命不忽木鞫之，具得其实，散札兒等伏诛，其捕系者尽释之。

translations.literal: The Chancellor entered his words in memorial; the Emperor understood, ordered Buhumu to try the case, fully obtained the truth; Sanzhar and the others were executed, and all who had been arrested and imprisoned were released.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor reported Buhumu's words to the throne. The Emperor saw the truth, ordered Buhumu to try the case, and the full facts came out. Sanzhar and his accomplices were executed, and all who had been arrested were released.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改工部尚书。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, he was transferred to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 九月，迁刑部。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, he was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 河东按察使阿合马，以赀财谄媚权贵，货钱于官，约偿羊马，至则抑取部民所产以输。

translations.literal: The Hedong Intendant Ahama, using wealth to flatter powerful men, borrowed money from the government with agreement to repay in sheep and horses; when payment came due, he forcibly seized what the people of his circuit produced to deliver it.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong intendant Ahama used his wealth to flatter the powerful. He borrowed money from the government on promise of repayment in sheep and horses, but when payment came due he forcibly seized the produce of local people to cover it.

sentences.zh: 事觉，遣使按治，皆不伏，及不忽木往，始得其不法百餘事。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, commissioners were dispatched to investigate; all denied guilt. Only when Buhumu went did they first obtain more than a hundred of his unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, investigators were sent, but all denied wrongdoing. Only when Buhumu went in person were more than a hundred of Ahama's unlawful acts uncovered.

sentences.zh: 会大同民饥，不忽木以便宜发仓廪赈之。

translations.literal: It happened that the people of Datong were starving; Buhumu on emergency authority opened the granaries and relief-grained them.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Datong suffered famine, Buhumu used his discretionary authority to open the granaries and provide relief.

sentences.zh: 阿合马所善幸臣奏不忽木擅发军储，又锻炼阿合马使自诬服。

translations.literal: A favorite minister on whom Ahama relied memorialized that Buhumu had on his own authority issued military stores; he also framed Ahama to make him falsely confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: A minister favored by Ahama memorialized that Buhumu had issued military stores on his own authority, and also framed Ahama to force a false confession.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「使行发粟以活吾民，乃其职也，何罪之有。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Sending grain to save our people — that is his duty. What crime is there?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Issuing grain to save our people is his duty. Where is the crime in that?"

sentences.zh: 命移其狱至京师审视，阿合马竟伏诛。

translations.literal: He ordered the case transferred to the capital for review; Ahama in the end was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the case transferred to the capital for review, and Ahama was ultimately executed.

sentences.zh: 吐土哈求钦察之为人奴者增益其军，而多取编民。

translations.literal: Tutuha requested that Kipchak persons who had been others' slaves be added to augment his army, while taking many registered civilians besides.
translations.idiomatic: Tutuha sought to augment his army with Kipchak men who had been others' slaves, but in the process he also enrolled many registered civilians.

sentences.zh: 中书佥省王遇验其籍改正之。

translations.literal: Wang Yu of the Secretariat checked the registers and corrected them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu of the Secretariat checked the registers and corrected the irregularities.

sentences.zh: 吐土哈遂奏遇有不臣语。

translations.literal: Tutuha thereupon memorialized that Yu had uttered disloyal words.
translations.idiomatic: Tutuha then memorialized that Wang Yu had spoken words of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲斩之，不忽木谏曰：「遇始令以钦察之人奴为兵，未闻以编民也。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and wanted to behead him. Buhumu remonstrated: "Yu at first had orders to take Kipchak persons who were others' slaves as soldiers — we have not heard of taking registered civilians.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and wanted to execute him. Buhumu remonstrated, "Wang Yu was originally ordered to enroll Kipchak men who had been others' slaves as soldiers — not registered civilians.

sentences.zh: 万一他卫皆仿此，户口耗矣。

translations.literal: If by chance every guard unit imitated this, household registers would be depleted.
translations.idiomatic: If every guard unit followed this example, the population registers would be depleted.

sentences.zh: 若诛遇，后人岂肯为陛下尽职乎？」

translations.literal: If Yu is executed, how will later men be willing to devote themselves to duty for Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: If Wang Yu is executed, who afterward will dare serve Your Majesty faithfully?"

sentences.zh: 帝意解，遇得不死。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind eased; Yu escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's anger subsided, and Wang Yu was spared.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，桑哥奏立尚书省，诬杀参政杨居宽、郭佑。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Sangge memorialized to establish the Ministry of State Affairs; he falsely charged and killed the Grand Councillors Yang Jukuan and Guo You.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, Sangge memorialized to establish the Ministry of State Affairs and had the grand councillors Yang Jukuan and Guo You falsely charged and executed.

sentences.zh: 不忽木争之不得，桑哥深忌之，尝指不忽木谓其妻曰：「他日籍我家者此人也。」

translations.literal: Buhumu argued against it without success. Sangge deeply resented him and once pointed at Buhumu and said to his wife: "The one who will confiscate our household on some future day is this man."
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu argued against it without success. Sangge came to hate him deeply and once pointed at Buhumu and told his wife, "This is the man who will one day confiscate our household."

sentences.zh: 因其退食，责以不坐曹理务，欲加之罪，遂以疾免。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of his leaving at mealtime, he charged him with not sitting at his desk handling affairs, seeking to attach guilt to him; thereupon on grounds of illness he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing on Buhumu's leaving at mealtimes, Sangge accused him of neglecting office duties and sought to attach guilt to him. Buhumu was then dismissed on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 车驾还自上都，其弟野礼审班侍坐辇中，帝曰：「汝兄必以某日来迎。」

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned from Shangdu, his younger brother Yelizhenban attended, sitting in the palanquin. The Emperor said: "Your elder brother will surely come to welcome on a certain day."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned from Shangdu, Buhumu's younger brother Yelizhenban sat in attendance within the carriage. The Emperor said, "Your elder brother will surely come to welcome us on a certain day."

sentences.zh: 不忽木果以是日至。

translations.literal: Buhumu indeed arrived on that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu did indeed arrive on that day.

sentences.zh: 帝见其癯甚，问其禄几何，左右对以满病假者例不给，帝念其贫，命尽给之。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw how emaciated he was, asked how much his salary was; attendants replied that those who had used up sick leave by regulation received none. The Emperor, mindful of his poverty, ordered it all granted.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how emaciated he was, the Emperor asked how much salary he received. Attendants replied that those who had exhausted sick leave received none by regulation. Mindful of Buhumu's poverty, the Emperor ordered his full salary restored.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，拜翰林学士承旨、知制诰兼修国史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he was appointed Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy, Drafter of Imperial Edicts, and concurrently compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, he was appointed academician expositor-in-chief of the Hanlin Academy, drafter of imperial edicts, and concurrently compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 二十八年春，帝猎柳林，彻里等劾奏桑哥罪状，帝召问不忽木，具以实对。

translations.literal: In spring of the twenty-eighth year, the Emperor hunted at Willow Grove. Cheli and others impeached Sangge, memorializing his crimes. The Emperor summoned and questioned Buhumu, who answered fully with the truth.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-eighth year, while the Emperor was hunting at Willow Grove, Cheli and others impeached Sangge and memorialized his crimes. The Emperor summoned Buhumu and questioned him; he answered with the full truth.

sentences.zh: 帝大惊，乃决意诛之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly shocked and thereupon resolved to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly shocked and resolved to have Sangge executed.

sentences.zh: 罢尚书省，复以六部归于中书，欲用不忽木为丞相，固辞，帝曰：「朕过听桑哥，致天下不安，今虽悔之，已无及矣。

translations.literal: The Ministry of State Affairs was abolished; the Six Ministries were returned to the Secretariat. He wished to use Buhumu as Chancellor; he firmly declined. The Emperor said: "I over-listened to Sangge and brought unrest to all under Heaven. Even if I regret it now, it is already too late.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of State Affairs was abolished and the Six Ministries restored to the Secretariat. The Emperor wished to appoint Buhumu chancellor, but he firmly declined. The Emperor said, "I listened too much to Sangge and brought unrest to the empire. Though I regret it now, it is already too late.

sentences.zh: 朕识卿幼时，使卿从学，政欲备今日之用，勿多让也。」

translations.literal: I knew you in your youth and had you follow studies — precisely intending to prepare you for use on a day like this. Do not decline overmuch."
translations.idiomatic: I knew you as a child and had you schooled precisely to prepare you for a day like this. Do not decline so much."

sentences.zh: 不忽木曰：「朝廷勋旧，齿爵居臣右者尚多，今不次用臣，无以服众。」

translations.literal: Buhumu said: "Meritorious elders of the court, many in age and rank stand to my right. To use me out of turn now — there is no way to win the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu said, "Many meritorious elders of the court still outrank me in age and rank. If you promote me out of turn, you will not win the assent of others."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然则孰可？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Then who is suitable?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Then who is suitable?"

sentences.zh: 对曰：「太子詹事完泽可。

translations.literal: He replied: "Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Wanze would do.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Wanze would be suitable.

sentences.zh: 向者籍没阿合马家，其赂遗近臣，皆有簿籍，唯无完泽名；

translations.literal: Previously when Ahama's household was confiscated, his bribes to close ministers all had ledgers — only Wanze's name was absent;
translations.idiomatic: When Ahama's household was confiscated earlier, ledgers recorded his bribes to court favorites — Wanze's name appeared on none of them;

sentences.zh: 又尝言桑哥为相，必败国事，今果如其言，是以知其可也。」

translations.literal: he also once said that with Sangge as chancellor, state affairs would surely be ruined — now it indeed matched his words; hence I know he is suitable."
translations.idiomatic: and he once said that Sangge as chancellor would ruin state affairs — which has now proved true. That is why I know he is suitable."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然非卿无以任吾事。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Yet without you there is no one to undertake my affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "But without you there is no one who can handle my affairs."

sentences.zh: 乃拜完泽右丞相，不忽木平章政事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wanze was appointed Right Chancellor and Buhumu Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wanze was appointed right chancellor and Buhumu grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 上都留守木八剌沙言改按察司置廉访司不便，宜罢去，乃求宪臣赃罪以动上听。

translations.literal: The Shangdu garrison commander Mubalasha said that changing the inspection commissions into integrity-visitation commissions was inconvenient and should be abolished; he then sought corrupt crimes of censorial officials to sway the Emperor's ear.
translations.idiomatic: The Shangdu garrison commander Mubalasha argued that converting the inspection commissions into integrity-visitation commissions was impracticable and should be abolished, and sought corrupt crimes among censorial officials to sway the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝以责中丞崔彧，彧谢病不知。

translations.literal: The Emperor blamed Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu for it; Yu pleaded illness and claimed ignorance.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor blamed Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu, who pleaded illness and claimed ignorance.

sentences.zh: 不忽木面斥彧不直言，因历陈不可罢之说，帝意乃释。

translations.literal: Buhumu face to face rebuked Yu for not speaking plainly, and in succession set forth the arguments against abolition; the Emperor's mind was then eased.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu rebuked Cui Yu to his face for failing to speak plainly, then set forth at length why the commissions should not be abolished, and the Emperor's doubts were resolved.

sentences.zh: 王师征交趾失利，复谋大举，不忽木曰：「岛夷诡诈，天威临之，宁不震惧，兽穷则噬，势使之然。

translations.literal: The imperial army's expedition against Jiaozhi failed; they again plotted a great campaign. Buhumu said: "The island barbarians are crafty; when Heaven's majesty presses upon them, would they not tremble with fear? A beast cornered will bite — circumstance makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial army's failed expedition against Jiaozhi, the court again planned a major campaign. Buhumu said, "The island peoples are crafty. When imperial majesty presses upon them, will they not tremble with fear? A cornered beast will bite — that is what circumstance drives them to do.

sentences.zh: 今其子日燇袭位，若遣一介之使，谕以祸福，彼能悔过自新，则不烦兵而下矣。

translations.literal: Now his son Ridian has succeeded to the throne; if one envoy is dispatched to instruct them on weal and woe, and they can repent and renew themselves, then without troubling the army they will submit.
translations.idiomatic: Now his son Ridian has succeeded to the throne. If a single envoy is sent to explain the consequences of fortune and disaster, and they repent and reform, they will submit without the trouble of armies.

sentences.zh: 如或不悛，加兵未晚。」

translations.literal: If they do not repent, sending troops will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: If they do not repent, it will not be too late to send troops."

sentences.zh: 帝从之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 于是交趾感惧，遣其伪昭明王等诣阙谢罪，尽献前六岁所当贡物。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiaozhi, moved by fear, sent its false King Zhaoming and others to the court to apologize for crimes, fully presenting the tribute goods due for the previous six years.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi, awed by fear, sent its envoy the so-called King Zhaoming and others to the court to apologize and submit the tribute owed for the previous six years in full.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「卿一言之力也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said with pleasure: "This is the power of a single word from you."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said with pleasure, "This is the power of a single word from you."

sentences.zh: 即以其半赐之，不忽木辞曰：「此陛下神武不杀所致，臣何功焉。」

translations.literal: He at once granted half to him as gift. Buhumu declined: "This comes from Your Majesty's divine martial power and sparing of lives — what merit have I?"
translations.idiomatic: He immediately offered Buhumu half of the tribute as a gift. Buhumu declined, saying, "This came about through Your Majesty's divine martial virtue and restraint from killing — what merit have I?"

sentences.zh: 惟受沉水假山、象牙镇纸、水晶笔格而已。

translations.literal: He accepted only an agarwood rockery, an ivory paperweight, and a crystal brush rack — that was all.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted only an agarwood rockery, an ivory paperweight, and a crystal brush rack — and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 麦术丁请复立尚书省，专领右三部，不忽木庭责之曰：「阿合马、桑哥相继误国，身诛家没，前鉴未远，奈何又欲效之乎！」

translations.literal: Maiduding requested re-establishing the Ministry of State Affairs to take exclusive charge of the right three departments. Buhumu rebuked him in open court: "Ahama and Sangge in succession misled the state, themselves executed and households destroyed — recent warning is not far; how then would you again wish to imitate them!"
translations.idiomatic: Maiduding requested re-establishing the Ministry of State Affairs to take exclusive charge of the three right departments. Buhumu rebuked him in open court: "Ahama and Sangge in succession misled the state and were executed with their households confiscated — the warning is still recent. How can you wish to repeat their example!"

sentences.zh: 事遂寝。

translations.literal: The matter thereupon was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was thereupon dropped.

sentences.zh: 或劝征流求，及赋江南包银，皆谏止之。

translations.literal: Some advised campaigns against Liuqiu and imposing the baoyin tax in Jiangnan; he remonstrated and stopped them all.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged campaigns against Liuqiu and the imposition of the baoyin tax in Jiangnan, he remonstrated and blocked both proposals.

sentences.zh: 桑哥党人纳速剌丁等既诛，帝以忻都长于理财，欲释不杀。

translations.literal: After Sangge's factionaries Nasir al-Din and others were executed, the Emperor, thinking Xindu excelled at managing finances, wished to spare him and not kill.
translations.idiomatic: After Sangge's followers Nasir al-Din and others were executed, the Emperor, believing Xindu excelled at fiscal management, wished to spare him.

sentences.zh: 不忽木力争之，不从。

translations.literal: Buhumu vigorously argued against it; the Emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu argued vigorously against it, but the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 日中凡七奏，卒正其罪。

translations.literal: Within the day he memorialized seven times in all; in the end the proper punishment was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single day he memorialized seven times, until at last the proper sentence was fixed.

sentences.zh: 释氏请以金银币帛祠其神，帝难之。

translations.literal: The Buddhist clergy requested gold, silver, silk, and cloth to sacrifice to their god; the Emperor found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist clergy requested gold, silver, silk, and cloth to sacrifice to their deity, and the Emperor was reluctant.

sentences.zh: 不忽木曰：「彼佛以去贪为宝。」

translations.literal: Buhumu said: "That Buddha takes relinquishing greed as treasure."
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu said, "The Buddha treasures the relinquishment of greed."

sentences.zh: 遂弗与。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was thereupon denied.

sentences.zh: 或言京师蒙古人宜与汉人间处，以制不虞。

translations.literal: Some said Mongols in the capital ought to live intermixed with Han people to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that Mongols in the capital should live intermixed with Han people as a precaution against unforeseen trouble.

sentences.zh: 不忽木曰：「新民乍迁，犹未宁居，若复纷更，必致失业。

translations.literal: Buhumu said: "New subjects have just moved; they are still not settled in dwelling. If there is further upheaval, they will surely lose livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu said, "The new subjects have only just moved and are not yet settled. Further upheaval will surely deprive them of their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 此盖奸人欲擅货易之利，交结近幸，借为纳忠之说耳。」

translations.literal: This surely is scoundrels wishing to monopolize the profits of trade, joining with close favorites and borrowing the guise of offering loyal counsel, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: This is surely the work of scoundrels who wish to monopolize trade profits, colluding with court favorites and dressing their scheme up as loyal counsel."

sentences.zh: 乃图写国中贵人第宅已与民居犬牙相制之状上之而止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drew and submitted a depiction showing how throughout the realm the mansions of the nobles and common dwellings already interlocked like dog's teeth checking each other — and the proposal stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a map showing how throughout the capital the mansions of the nobility already interlocked with common dwellings like teeth in a jaw — and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 有谮完泽徇私者，帝以问不忽木。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Wanze for favoritism; the Emperor asked Buhumu.
translations.idiomatic: When someone slandered Wanze for favoritism, the Emperor asked Buhumu about it.

sentences.zh: 对曰：「完泽与臣俱待罪中书，设或如所言，岂得专行。

translations.literal: He replied: "Wanze and I both await blame at the Secretariat; if it were as said, how could he act alone?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Wanze and I both serve at the Secretariat under shared responsibility. If things were as alleged, how could he act alone?

sentences.zh: 臣等虽愚陋，然备位宰辅，人或发其阴短，宜使面质，明示责降，若内怀猜疑，非人主至公之道也。」

translations.literal: Although we ministers are dull and lowly, we yet fill the seats of chief ministers. When someone brings out another's hidden faults, he ought to be made to face that person and confront the matter; responsibility should be clearly shown and reduced. If one harbors suspicion within, that is not the way of utmost fairness for a lord of men."
translations.idiomatic: Though we ministers are unremarkable men, we hold the highest offices of state. When someone is accused of hidden faults, he ought to be brought face to face with his accuser and the charge openly examined. To act on secret suspicion alone is not the way of a truly just sovereign."

sentences.zh: 言者果屈，帝怒，命左右批其颊而出之。

translations.literal: The accuser was indeed refuted. The Emperor was angry and ordered attendants to strike his cheeks and drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: The slanderer was indeed refuted. The Emperor was angry and ordered his attendants to slap the man's cheeks and drive him out.

sentences.zh: 是日苦寒，解所御黑貂裘以赐。

translations.literal: That day was bitterly cold; [the Emperor] removed his own black sable fur coat and conferred it as gift.
translations.idiomatic: That day was bitterly cold; the Emperor took off his own black sable fur coat and bestowed it on Buhumu.

sentences.zh: 帝每顾侍臣，称塞咥旃之能，不忽木从容问其故，帝曰：「彼事宪宗，常阴资朕财用，卿父所知。

translations.literal: The Emperor whenever turned to attending ministers praised Saidian Zhan's ability. Buhumu calmly asked the reason. The Emperor said: "He served Möngke Khan and secretly supplied my finances — your father knew of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would often turn to his attending ministers and praise Saidian Zhan's abilities. Buhumu calmly asked why. The Emperor said, "When he served Möngke Khan, he secretly supplied me with funds — your father knew of this.

sentences.zh: 卿时未生，诚不知也。」

translations.literal: At that time you were not yet born; you truly do not know.
translations.idiomatic: You had not yet been born; you truly would not know.

sentences.zh: 不忽木曰：「是所谓为人臣怀二心者。

translations.literal: Buhumu said: "That is what is called a minister who harbors two hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu said, "That is what we call a minister who serves two masters.

sentences.zh: 今有以内府财物私结亲王，陛下以为若何？」

translations.literal: Now suppose someone privately wins over a prince with inner-palace goods — what does Your Majesty think of that?
translations.idiomatic: If someone were now to use imperial treasury goods to cultivate a prince in secret, what would Your Majesty think of that?

sentences.zh: 帝急挥以手曰：「卿止，朕失言。」

translations.literal: The Emperor hastily waved his hand and said: "Stop — I spoke amiss.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hastily waved his hand. "Enough," he said. "I spoke out of turn.

sentences.zh: 三十年，有星孛于帝座。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, a broom star appeared at the Emperor's Throne constellation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1293), a comet appeared near the Imperial Throne constellation.

sentences.zh: 帝忧之，夜召入禁中，问所以销天变之道，奏曰：「风雨自天而至，人则栋宇以待之；

translations.literal: The Emperor worried about it; at night he summoned [Buhumu] into the inner palace and asked the way to dispel heavenly portents. He memorialized: "Wind and rain come from Heaven — men build roofs and halls to await them;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was troubled. At night he summoned Buhumu into the inner palace and asked how to avert the heavenly omen. Buhumu replied, "Wind and rain descend from Heaven — and men build roofs and halls to receive them;

sentences.zh: 江河为地之限，人则舟楫以通之。

translations.literal: Rivers form the boundaries of the earth — men use boats and oars to traverse them.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers mark the boundaries of the land — and men build boats to cross them.

sentences.zh: 天地有所不能者，人则为之，此人所以与天地参也。

translations.literal: What Heaven and Earth cannot do, men do — this is why humans are ranked alongside Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Where Heaven and Earth fall short, men must act — and that is how humans share in the work of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 且父母怒，人子不敢疾怨，惟起敬起孝。

translations.literal: Moreover, when parents are angry, a human child dares not resent quickly — he can only raise reverence and raise filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When a parent is angry, a dutiful child does not dare resent it — he can only respond with reverence and filial devotion.
