sentences.zh: 故《易·震》之象曰『君子以恐惧修省』，《诗》曰『敬天之怒』，又曰『遇灾而惧』。

translations.literal: Thus the Image of Thunder in the Book of Changes says, "The noble man, in fear and trembling, cultivates self-examination." The Book of Songs says, "Revere Heaven's anger," and again says, "When meeting disaster, be fearful."
translations.idiomatic: The Image of Thunder in the Book of Changes enjoins: "The noble man, in fear and trembling, examines himself." The Book of Songs says, "Revere Heaven's wrath," and again: "When calamity strikes, be afraid."

sentences.zh: 三代圣王，克谨天戒，鲜不有终。

translations.literal: The sage kings of the Three Dynasties, able to heed Heaven's warnings, few lacked good endings.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of the Three Dynasties who heeded Heaven's warnings rarely failed to meet a good end.

sentences.zh: 汉文之世，同日山崩者二十有九，日食地震频岁有之，善用此道，天亦悔祸，海内乂安。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Wen of Han, on the same day mountains collapsed twenty-nine times; eclipses and earthquakes occurred year after year. By skillfully using this way, Heaven too repented of calamity and within the seas all was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Han, twenty-nine mountains collapsed on the same day, and eclipses and earthquakes came year after year. By following this course, Heaven itself relented, and the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 此前代之龟鉴也，臣愿陛下法之。」

translations.literal: These are the tortoise mirrors of former ages — your subject wishes Your Majesty to take them as law.
translations.idiomatic: These are the lessons of the past, Your Majesty — I urge you to follow their example.

sentences.zh: 因诵文帝《日食求言诏》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recited Emperor Wen's Edict on Seeking Counsel at a Solar Eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: He then recited Emperor Wen's edict calling for remonstrance after a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 帝悚然曰：「此言深合朕意，可复诵之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor startled said: "These words deeply accord with my intent — you may recite them again.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was shaken. "Your words strike deeply at my heart," he said. "Recite them again.

sentences.zh: 遂详论款陈，夜至四鼓，明日进膳，帝以盘珍赐之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he discussed in detail and set forth earnestly; the night reached the fourth watch. Next day at the meal offering, the Emperor conferred plate-delicacies on him.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu then expounded at length, and the audience lasted until the fourth watch. The next morning at breakfast, the Emperor presented him with delicacies from his own table.

sentences.zh: 三十年，帝不豫，故事，非国人勋旧不得入卧内。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the Emperor was unwell. By precedent, unless one was a countryman of meritorious old standing one could not enter the bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: In that thirtieth year the Emperor fell ill. By established custom, only Mongols of old merit were permitted to enter the royal bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 不忽木以谨厚，日视医药，未尝去左右。

translations.literal: Buhumu, because of his careful dutifulness, daily attended to medicines and never left the Emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his steadfast loyalty, Buhumu attended him daily, supervising his medicine and never leaving his side.

sentences.zh: 帝大渐，与御史大夫月鲁那颜、太傅伯颜并受遗诏，留禁中。

translations.literal: As the Emperor's condition grew critical, together with Censor-in-Chief Yelü Nayin and Grand Preceptor Bayan he together received the deathbed edict and remained in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor's condition turned critical, Buhumu, together with Censor-in-Chief Yelü Nayin and Grand Preceptor Bayan, received the deathbed testament and remained in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 丞相完泽至，不得入，伺月鲁那颜、伯颜出，问曰：「我年位俱在不忽木上，国有大议而不预，何耶？」

translations.literal: Grand Chancellor Wanze arrived but could not enter; waiting until Yelü Nayin and Bayan came out, he asked: "My age and rank are both above Buhumu's — there is a great deliberation for the state yet I am not included; why?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Chancellor Wanze arrived but was refused entry. When Yelü Nayin and Bayan emerged, he asked, "I am both older and senior in rank to Buhumu — yet I am excluded from a deliberation of state importance. Why?

sentences.zh: 伯颜叹息曰：「使丞相有不忽木识虑，何至使吾属如是之劳哉！」

translations.literal: Bayan sighed and said: "If the Grand Chancellor had Buhumu's insight and deliberation, how could we have been put to such labor!
translations.idiomatic: Bayan sighed. "If the Grand Chancellor had Buhumu's insight," he said, "we would never have been burdened with such labor!

sentences.zh: 完泽不能对，入言于太后。

translations.literal: Wanze could not reply; he entered and spoke to the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Wanze had no answer and went in to speak with the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后召三人问之，月鲁那颜曰：「臣受顾命，太后但观臣等为之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager summoned the three and questioned them. Yelü Nayin said: "Your subject received the dying charge — the Empress Dowager need only observe us carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager summoned the three men and questioned them. Yelü Nayin said, "We received the Emperor's final charge. Your Majesty need only watch us fulfill it.

sentences.zh: 臣若误国，即日伏诛，宗社大事，非宫中所当预知也。」

translations.literal: If your subject errs against the state, on that same day let him submit to execution. The great affairs of altars and grain are not what the inner palace ought to foreknow.
translations.idiomatic: If we fail the state, execute us that very day. Affairs of dynasty and realm are not matters the inner palace should learn of in advance.

sentences.zh: 太后然其言，遂定大策。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager approved his words and thereupon settled the great policy.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager accepted this, and the great decision was settled.

sentences.zh: 其后发引、升祔、请谥南郊，皆不忽木领之。

translations.literal: Thereafter the departure of the coffin, elevation for joint burial, and petitioning for posthumous title at the Southern Altar — all were led by Buhumu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Buhumu oversaw the funeral procession, the enshrinement rites, and the petition for a posthumous title at the Southern Altar.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，执政皆迎于上都之北。

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne, those in power all went to welcome him north of Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong ascended the throne, the chief ministers all went north of Shangdu to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 丞相常独入，不忽木至数日乃得见，帝问知之，慰劳之曰：「卿先朝腹心，顾朕寡昧，惟朝夕启沃，以匡朕不逮，庶无负先帝付托之重也。」

translations.literal: The Grand Chancellor constantly entered alone; Buhumu only after several days was able to see him. The Emperor, learning of this, consoled and commended him, saying: "You are a trusted confidant of the previous court. Consider that I am young and ignorant — only morning and evening instruct and nourish me to correct my shortcomings, so that perhaps I may not fail the heavy charge the late Emperor entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Chancellor was admitted alone, while Buhumu waited several days before he could see the new Emperor. When Chengzong learned of this, he sought Buhumu out and said, "You were my father's most trusted adviser. I am young and untested — instruct me day and night, correct my failings, that I may not betray the weight of trust my father placed in us both.

sentences.zh: 成宗躬揽庶政，听断明果，廷议大事多采不忽木之言。

translations.literal: Chengzong personally took hold of routine governance; his judgments were clear and decisive, and in court deliberations on great affairs he often adopted Buhumu's words.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong personally handled affairs of state. His judgments were swift and clear, and in deliberations on weighty matters the court often followed Buhumu's counsel.

sentences.zh: 太后亦以不忽木先朝旧臣，礼貌甚至。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager also, because Buhumu was an old minister of the previous court, showed courtesy to an extreme degree.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager likewise treated Buhumu, as a veteran minister of the previous reign, with the utmost respect.

sentences.zh: 河东守臣献嘉禾，大臣欲奏以为瑞。

translations.literal: The defending official of Hedong presented auspicious grain; great ministers wished to memorialize it as an omen.
translations.idiomatic: The governor of Hedong presented stalks of extraordinary grain, and senior ministers proposed reporting it to the throne as an auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 不忽木语之曰：「汝部内所产尽然耶，惟此数茎耶？」

translations.literal: Buhumu said to him: "Within your department, is everything produced thus, or only these few stalks?
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu asked him, "Did your entire province produce such grain — or only these few stalks?

sentences.zh: 曰：「惟此数茎尔。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Only these few stalks, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Only these few stalks.

sentences.zh: 不忽木曰：「若如此，既无益于民，又何足为瑞。」

translations.literal: Buhumu said: "If so, since it benefits the people not at all, how can it be worth calling an omen?
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu said, "If that is so, it brings no benefit to the people — how can it count as an auspicious omen?

sentences.zh: 遂罢遣之。

translations.literal: Thereupon [the proposal] was dropped and he was sent away.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped and the envoy dismissed.

sentences.zh: 西僧为佛事，请释罪人祈福，谓之秃鲁麻。

translations.literal: Western monks, performing Buddhist rites, requested releasing criminals to pray for blessings — this was called tuluoma.
translations.idiomatic: Western Buddhist monks performing religious rites requested the release of criminals to earn merit — a practice called tuluoma.

sentences.zh: 豪民犯法者，皆贿赂之以求免。

translations.literal: Wealthy commoners who violated the law all bribed them to seek exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy lawbreakers bribed the monks to secure their release.

sentences.zh: 有杀主、杀夫者，西僧请被以帝后御服，乘黄犊出宫门释之，云可得福。

translations.literal: There were murderers of masters and murderers of husbands; Western monks requested they be clothed in imperial and empress consort's ceremonial dress, ride a yellow calf out the palace gate, and be released — saying thereby fortune could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Murderers of masters and husbands alike — the monks would dress them in robes reserved for the Emperor and Empress, seat them on yellow calves, and escort them out the palace gates to freedom, claiming the act would earn divine blessing.

sentences.zh: 不忽木曰：「人伦者，王政之本，风化之基，岂可容其乱法如是！」

translations.literal: Buhumu said: "Human relations are the root of royal government, the foundation of customs and transformation — how can such lawlessness be tolerated!
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu protested, "Human relationships are the foundation of governance and the bedrock of public morals — how can we tolerate such contempt for the law!

sentences.zh: 帝责丞相曰：「朕戒汝无使不忽木知，今闻其言，朕甚愧之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked the Grand Chancellor: "I charged you not to let Buhumu know — now I hear his words, and I am greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked the Grand Chancellor. "I told you to keep this from Buhumu," he said. "Now I have heard what he says, and I am deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 使人谓不忽木曰：「卿且休矣！

translations.literal: He sent someone to tell Buhumu: "Rest for now!
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Buhumu: "Let the matter rest for now.

sentences.zh: 朕今从卿言，然自是以为故事。」

translations.literal: I now follow your words — yet from this time forward let it be taken as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: I accept your counsel this once — but hereafter it shall remain established custom.

sentences.zh: 有奴告主者，主被诛，诏即以其主所居官与之。

translations.literal: There was a slave who denounced his master; the master was executed, and an edict immediately conferred on him the office his master had held.
translations.idiomatic: When a slave denounced his master and the master was executed, an edict immediately granted the slave his master's official position.

sentences.zh: 不忽木言：「若此必大坏天下之风俗，使人情愈薄，无复上下之分矣。」

translations.literal: Buhumu said: "If it is thus, it will greatly ruin the customs of the realm, make human sentiment ever thinner, and there will no longer be distinction between superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu objected, "Such a policy will destroy public morality, erode all bonds of loyalty, and obliterate the distinction between high and low.

sentences.zh: 帝悟，为追废前命。

translations.literal: The Emperor understood and revoked the prior order.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor saw the wisdom of this and revoked his earlier edict.

sentences.zh: 执政奏以为陕西行省平章政事，太后谓帝曰：「不忽木朝廷正人，先皇帝所付托，岂可出之于外耶！」

translations.literal: Those in power memorialized appointing him Grand Councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat. The Empress Dowager told the Emperor: "Buhumu is an upright man of the court — the late Emperor entrusted him; how can he be sent outside!
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers recommended appointing Buhumu Grand Councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat. The Empress Dowager told the Emperor, "Buhumu is the conscience of this court — your father entrusted the realm to him. How can you send him away?

sentences.zh: 帝复留之。

translations.literal: The Emperor again kept him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor kept him at court.

sentences.zh: 竟以与同列多异议，称疾不出。

translations.literal: In the end, because he had many points of disagreement with fellow ministers, he claimed illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, finding himself at odds with his fellow ministers on too many matters, he pleaded illness and withdrew from court.

sentences.zh: 元贞二年春，召至便殿曰：「朕知卿疾之故，以卿不能从人，人亦不能从卿也。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Yuanzhen, [the Emperor] summoned him to the side hall and said: "I know the cause of your illness — because you cannot follow others, others also cannot follow you.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1296, the Emperor summoned him to the side hall. "I understand the cause of your illness," he said. "You cannot follow others — and others cannot follow you.

sentences.zh: 欲以段贞代卿，如何？」

translations.literal: I wish to replace you with Duan Zhen — how would that be?
translations.idiomatic: I propose to replace you with Duan Zhen. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 不忽木曰：「贞实胜于臣。」

translations.literal: Buhumu said: "Zhen is truly superior to your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Buhumu replied, "Duan Zhen is indeed the better man.

sentences.zh: 乃拜昭文馆大学士、平章军国重事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall and Grand Councillor for Important Military and State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall and Grand Councillor for Military and State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 辞曰：「是职也，国朝惟史天泽尝为之，臣何功敢当此。」

translations.literal: He declined, saying: "That office — in our dynasty only Shi Tianze once held it; what merit has your subject to dare accept this?
translations.idiomatic: He declined, saying, "In our dynasty only Shi Tianze has held that office. What merit have I to dare accept it?

sentences.zh: 制去「重」字。

translations.literal: The appointment removed the character "Important."
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was revised to drop the word "Important" from the title.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，御史中丞崔彧卒，特命行中丞事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu died; [Buhumu] was specially ordered to perform the censor-in-chief's duties.
translations.idiomatic: In 1298, when Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu died, Buhumu was specially ordered to act in his stead.

sentences.zh: 三年，兼领侍仪司事。

translations.literal: In the third year, he concurrently took charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was additionally placed in charge of the Directorate of Court Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 有因父官受贿赂，御史必欲归罪其父，不忽木曰：「风纪之司，以宣政化、励风俗为先，若使子证父，何以兴孝！」

translations.literal: There was a case where someone because of his father's office took bribes; the censor insisted on assigning guilt to the father. Buhumu said: "The office of wind and discipline takes spreading political transformation and encouraging custom as foremost — if one makes the son testify against the father, how can filial piety be raised!
translations.idiomatic: When a man took bribes through his father's office and the censor insisted on charging the father, Buhumu said, "The Censorate exists to uphold policy and encourage proper conduct. If we compel a son to testify against his father, how can we promote filial piety!

sentences.zh: 枢密臣受人玉带，征赃不叙，御史言罚太轻，不忽木曰：「礼，大臣贪墨，惟曰簠簋不饰，若加笞辱，非刑不上大夫之意。」

translations.literal: A Privy Council minister received someone else's jade belt; after recovery of illicit goods he was not reappointed. The censor said the penalty was too light. Buhumu said: "By ritual, when a great minister is corrupt, one says only that the vessels are not polished — if one adds beating and humiliation, that is not the meaning of 'punishment does not reach up to the Grandee.'
translations.idiomatic: When a Privy Council minister accepted a jade belt as a bribe and, after restitution, was merely barred from office, the censor protested that the penalty was too lenient. Buhumu said, "By ritual propriety, a corrupt minister is rebuked with the phrase 'his vessels are unpolished.' To add beating and public humiliation violates the principle that punishment does not reach up to the Grandee.

sentences.zh: 人称其平恕。

translations.literal: People praised his evenness and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: People praised his fairness and moderation.

sentences.zh: 四年，病复作，帝遣医治之，不效，乃附奏曰：「臣孱庸无取，叨承眷渥，大限有终，永辞昭代。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, illness recurred; the Emperor sent physicians to treat him — without effect. He then attached a memorial: "Your subject is feeble and worthless, undeservedly receiving gracious favor; the great limit has its end — forever bidding farewell to the bright age.
translations.idiomatic: In 1300 his illness returned. The Emperor sent physicians, but to no avail. Buhumu submitted a final memorial: "Your worthless subject has enjoyed undeserved favor; my appointed span is ended, and I take everlasting leave of this enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 引觞满饮而卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: He raised the cup, drank it full, and died — age forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his cup, drained it, and died. He was forty-six.

sentences.zh: 帝闻之惊悼，士大夫皆哭失声。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he was startled and grieved; scholar-officials all wept beyond voice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was stricken with grief, and the scholar-officials wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 家素贫，躬自爨汲，妻织纴以养母。

translations.literal: His household was always poor; he personally cooked and drew water; his wife wove hemp to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His family had always been poor. He cooked and drew water himself; his wife wove cloth to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 后因使还，则母已死，号恸呕血，几不起。

translations.literal: Later, returning from a mission, he found his mother already dead; he wailed and vomited blood, nearly not rising.
translations.idiomatic: Once, returning from an official mission, he found his mother already dead. He wailed until he vomited blood and nearly died of grief.

sentences.zh: 平居服儒素，不尚华饰。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he wore Confucian simplicity and did not esteem ornate display.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he dressed plainly in the Confucian style and scorned ornament.

sentences.zh: 禄赐有餘，即散施亲旧。

translations.literal: When salary and gifts had surplus, he at once distributed them to kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his salary and gifts exceeded his needs, he gave the surplus to relatives and old friends.

sentences.zh: 明于知人，多所荐拔，丞相哈剌哈孙答剌罕亦其所荐也。

translations.literal: Clear in knowing men, he recommended and elevated many; Grand Chancellor Qalaqsun Dalan was also one he recommended.
translations.idiomatic: He had a keen eye for talent and recommended many men for office — Grand Chancellor Qalaqsun Dalan among them.

sentences.zh: 其学先躬行而后文艺。

translations.literal: His learning put personal conduct first and literary arts after.
translations.idiomatic: In his learning he placed moral conduct above literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 居则简默，及帝前论事，吐辞洪暢，引义正大，以天下之重自任，知无不言。

translations.literal: At rest he was brief and silent; before the Emperor discussing affairs his words poured forth grandly and smoothly, citations righteous and great, taking the weight of the realm upon himself — what he knew he did not fail to speak.
translations.idiomatic: In private he was quiet and reserved; before the Emperor he spoke with force and clarity, citing principle with unwavering rectitude. He took the welfare of the realm as his personal charge and held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 世祖尝语之曰：「太祖有言，人主理天下，如右手持物，必资左手承之，然后能固。

translations.literal: Kublai once said to him: "Taizu had a saying — the lord of men governing the realm is like the right hand holding a thing; he must rely on the left hand to support it — only then can it be firm.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai once told him, "Taizu said: governing the realm is like holding something in the right hand — you need the left hand to steady it, or the grip will fail.

sentences.zh: 卿实朕之左手也。」

translations.literal: You truly are my left hand.
translations.idiomatic: You are truly my left hand.

sentences.zh: 每侍燕间，必陈说古今治要，世祖每拊髀叹曰：「恨卿生晚，不得早闻此言，然亦吾子孙之福。」

translations.literal: Whenever attending at leisure feasts he invariably set forth the essential points of governance ancient and modern; Kublai each time slapped his thigh and sighed: "I regret you were born late — I could not hear these words early — yet it is also fortune for my descendants.
translations.idiomatic: At every informal audience Buhumu would expound the essentials of governance, ancient and modern. Kublai would slap his thigh and sigh, "I regret you came to me so late — yet my descendants will be the richer for it.

sentences.zh: 临崩，以白璧遗之，曰：「他日持此以见朕也。」

translations.literal: At impending death, he bequeathed to him a white jade disc, saying: "Another day hold this to see me.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Kublai left Buhumu a white jade disc, saying, "Keep this — one day bring it when you come to see me again.

sentences.zh: 武宗时，赠纯诚佐理功臣、太傅、开府仪同三司、上柱国、鲁国公，谥文贞。

translations.literal: In Wuzong's time, he was posthumously granted Pure Loyalty Assisting Governance Meritorious Subject, Grand Preceptor, Grand Prefect with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of the State, Duke of Lu — posthumous title Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuzong he was posthumously ennobled as Pure Loyalty, Assisting Governance Meritorious Subject, Grand Preceptor, and Duke of Lu with the posthumous name Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子回回，陕西行省平章政事；

translations.literal: His son Huihui, Grand Councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: His son Huihui served as Grand Councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 巙巙，由江浙行省平章政事入为翰林学士承旨。

translations.literal: Ququ, from Grand Councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat entered service as Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ququ rose from Grand Councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat to Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: ○完泽

translations.literal: ○ Wanze
translations.idiomatic: Wanze

sentences.zh: 完泽，土别燕氏。

translations.literal: Wanze, of the Tübiyan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wanze was of the Tübiyan clan.

sentences.zh: 祖土薛，从太祖起朔方，平诸部。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tüshe followed Taizu rising from the northern frontier and pacified the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tüshe followed Taizu from the northern frontier and helped pacify the tribes.

sentences.zh: 太宗伐金，命太弟睿宗由陕右进师，以击其不备，土薛为先锋，遂去武休关，越汉江，略方城而北，破金兵于阳翟。

translations.literal: Taizong campaigning against Jin ordered the Great Younger Brother Ruizong to advance from the Shaanxi right flank to strike their unpreparedness; Tüshe was vanguard, then departed Wuxiu Pass, crossed the Han River, raided Fangcheng and turned north, defeating Jin troops at Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: When Ögedei invaded Jin, he ordered Prince Ruizong to advance through Shaanxi and strike where the enemy was unready. Tüshe served as vanguard, broke through Wuxiu Pass, crossed the Han River, swept through Fangcheng, and routed Jin forces at Yangzhai.

sentences.zh: 金亡，从攻兴元、阆、利诸州，拜都元帅。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, he followed in attacking Xingyuan, Lang, Li, and other prefectures, and was appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Jin he joined campaigns against Xingyuan, Lang, Li, and other prefectures, and was appointed Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 取宋成都，斩其将陈隆之，赐食邑六百户。

translations.literal: He captured Song Chengdu, beheaded its general Chen Longzhi, and was granted a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Song city of Chengdu, executed the Song general Chen Longzhi, and was granted a fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 父纟泉真，宿卫禁中，掌御膳。

translations.literal: His father Wozhen served as imperial guard in the forbidden precincts and managed the imperial diet.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wozhen served in the inner guard and managed the imperial kitchens.

sentences.zh: 中统初，从世祖北征。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong, he followed Kublai on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhongtong era (1260), he joined Kublai's northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜中书右丞相，与诸儒臣论定朝制。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Right Grand Chancellor of the Secretariat and with various Confucian ministers deliberated and fixed court institutions.
translations.idiomatic: In 1263 he was appointed Right Grand Chancellor of the Secretariat and, together with Confucian advisers, helped establish the court's institutions.

sentences.zh: 完泽以大臣子选为裕宗王府僚属。

translations.literal: Wanze, as a great minister's son, was selected as a staff member of Prince Yuzong's princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wanze, as the son of a senior minister, was selected to serve on the staff of Prince Yuzong's household.

sentences.zh: 裕宗为皇太子，署詹事长。

translations.literal: When Yuzong became Crown Prince, [Wanze] was appointed Chief Steward.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuzong was installed as Crown Prince, Wanze was named Chief Steward of his household.

sentences.zh: 入参谋议，出掌环卫，小心慎密，太子甚器重之。

translations.literal: Within he joined deliberation and counsel; without he managed guard and escort — careful and meticulous; the Crown Prince greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He advised the prince on policy within the palace and commanded his guard without. Meticulous and trustworthy, he won the Crown Prince's deep confidence.

sentences.zh: 一日会燕宗室，指完泽语众曰：「亲善远恶，君之急务。

translations.literal: One day, gathering clan members at a banquet, [the Crown Prince] pointed at Wanze and told the assembly: "Drawing near the good and keeping the wicked at a distance — these are a lord's urgent tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Once, at a gathering of the imperial clan, the Crown Prince pointed to Wanze and told the assembly, "Drawing near the virtuous and keeping the wicked at a distance — these are a ruler's first duties.

sentences.zh: 善人如完泽者，群臣中岂易得哉！」

translations.literal: A good man like Wanze — among all ministers how easily obtained is he!
translations.idiomatic: A man like Wanze is not easily found among all the officials!

sentences.zh: 自是常典东宫卫兵。

translations.literal: From then on [Wanze] regularly held standard charge of the Eastern Palace guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wanze regularly commanded the Crown Prince's guard.

sentences.zh: 裕宗薨，成宗以皇孙抚军北方，完泽两从入北。

translations.literal: When Yuzong died, Chengzong as imperial grandson held troops in the north; Wanze twice followed in entering the north.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuzong's death, Chengzong as imperial grandson took command in the north, and Wanze accompanied him on both northern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 至元二十八年，桑哥伏诛，世祖咨问廷臣，特拜中书右丞相。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan, Sangge was executed; Kublai consulted court ministers and specially appointed [Wanze] Right Grand Chancellor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1291, after Sangge's execution, Kublai consulted the court and specially appointed Wanze Right Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 完泽入相，革桑哥弊政，请自中统初积岁逋负之钱粟，悉蠲免之，民赖其惠。

translations.literal: Wanze entering as chancellor reformed Sangge's corrupt policies, requesting from Zhongtong's beginning accumulated years of overdue money and grain — all fully remitted; the people relied on his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, Wanze abolished Sangge's abusive policies and petitioned to remit all taxes and grain levies in arrears since the beginning of the Zhongtong era. The people benefited greatly from his relief.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，世祖崩，完泽受遗诏，合宗戚大臣之议，启皇太后，迎成宗即位，诏谕中外，罢征安南之师，建议加上祖宗尊谥庙号，致养皇太后，示天下为人子之礼。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Kublai died; Wanze received the deathbed edict, combined deliberations of clansmen and great ministers, informed the Empress Dowager, welcomed Chengzong to the throne, issued an edict to inner and outer realms, halted the campaign against Annam, proposed adding honorific posthumous titles and temple names to ancestors and forebears, attended to nourishing the Empress Dowager, displaying to the realm the rites of being a human child.
translations.idiomatic: In 1294, when Kublai died, Wanze received the deathbed testament. Conferring with the imperial clan and senior ministers, he informed the Empress Dowager and installed Chengzong on the throne. He issued proclamations throughout the realm, recalled the army from Annam, proposed honorific posthumous titles for the imperial ancestors, and set an example of filial devotion to the Empress Dowager for the entire empire.

sentences.zh: 元贞以来，朝廷恪守成宪，诏书屡下散财发粟，不惜巨万，以颁赐百姓，当时以贤相称之。

translations.literal: From Yuanzhen onward, the court strictly observed established statutes; edicts repeatedly issued distributing wealth and releasing grain, sparing not tens of thousands, to bestow upon the common people — at the time he was regarded as worthy chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yuanzhen era onward the court adhered faithfully to established law. Edicts poured forth distributing treasure and grain to the people without stint, and at the time Wanze was widely praised as a worthy chancellor.

sentences.zh: 大德四年，加太傅、录军国重事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade, [he was] additionally appointed Grand Tutor and charged with recording matters of military and state import.
translations.idiomatic: In 1300 he was further appointed Grand Tutor and entrusted with overseeing affairs of military and state importance.

sentences.zh: 位望益崇，成宗倚任之意益重，而能处之以安静，不急于功利，故吏民守职乐业，世称贤相云。

translations.literal: Rank and prestige grew ever loftier; Chengzong's trust in him grew ever deeper — yet he maintained himself in quiet steadiness, not pressing for quick profit or achievement. Therefore officials and commoners kept their posts and took satisfaction in their work; the age hailed him as a worthy chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: His rank and prestige rose ever higher, and Chengzong relied on him more heavily still. Yet Wanze conducted himself with quiet steadiness, never pressing for quick profit or visible achievement. Officials and commoners kept to their duties in contentment, and the age hailed him as a worthy chancellor.

sentences.zh: 七年薨，年五十八，追封兴元王，谥忠宪。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, aged fifty-eight; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xingyuan, with posthumous title Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1303, aged fifty-eight. Posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xingyuan, he was given the posthumous title Loyal and Lawful.

sentences.zh: ○阿鲁浑萨理

translations.literal: ○ Aluhunsali
translations.idiomatic: Aluhunsali

sentences.zh: 阿鲁浑萨理，畏兀人。

translations.literal: Aluhunsali was a Uighur.
translations.idiomatic: Aluhunsali was a Uighur.

sentences.zh: 祖阿台萨理，当太祖定西域还时，因从至燕。

translations.literal: His grandfather Atai Sali, when Taizu returned from pacifying the Western Regions, followed him to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Atai Sali followed Taizu to Yan when the founder returned from pacifying the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 会畏兀国王亦都护请于朝，尽归其民，诏许之，遂复西还。

translations.literal: It happened that the Uighur king Idikut petitioned the court to fully restore his people; an edict granted it, and [Atai Sali] then returned west again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uighur king Idikut petitioned the court to restore his people in full, the request was granted by edict, and Atai Sali returned west.

sentences.zh: 精佛氏学。

translations.literal: He was accomplished in Buddhist learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply versed in Buddhist learning.

sentences.zh: 生乞台萨理，袭先业，通经、律、论。

translations.literal: He fathered Qitai Sali, who inherited the ancestral calling and mastered the sutras, vinaya, and shastras.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son, Qitai Sali, who inherited the family vocation and mastered the sutras, monastic discipline, and treatises.

sentences.zh: 业既成，师名之曰万全。

translations.literal: When his training was complete, his teacher named him Wanquan.
translations.idiomatic: When his training was complete, his teacher gave him the name Wanquan, Wholly Complete.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，入为释教都总统，拜正议大夫、同知总制院事，加资德大夫、统制使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan he entered service as Overall President of the Buddhist clergy, was appointed Righteousness Discussion Grandee and Associate Director of the Directorate for General Regulation, and additionally made Virtuous Virtue Grandee and Regulatory Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 he entered court service as Overall President of the Buddhist clergy, was appointed Righteousness Discussion Grandee and associate director of the Directorate for General Regulation, and was further promoted to Virtuous Virtue Grandee and regulatory commissioner.

sentences.zh: 年七十卒。

translations.literal: He died at seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 子三人：长曰畏吾兒萨理，累官资德大夫、中书右丞、行泉府太卿；

translations.literal: He had three sons: the eldest was Weiwu'er Sali, who rose to Virtuous Virtue Grandee, Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and Acting Director of the Directorate of the Treasury;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons. The eldest, Weiwu'er Sali, rose to Virtuous Virtue Grandee, right vice minister of the Secretariat, and acting director of the Directorate of the Treasury;

sentences.zh: 季曰岛瓦赤萨理；

translations.literal: the youngest was Diaowachi Sali;
translations.idiomatic: the youngest was Diaowachi Sali;

sentences.zh: 阿鲁浑萨理，其中子也，以父字为全氏，幼聪慧，受业于国师八哈思巴，既通其学，且解诸国语。

translations.literal: Aluhunsali was the middle son. Taking his father's courtesy name, he used the surname Quan. Bright from childhood, he studied under State Preceptor Phagspa, mastered that learning, and also understood the various national languages.
translations.idiomatic: Aluhunsali was the middle son. He took his father's courtesy name and bore the surname Quan. Bright from childhood, he studied under State Preceptor Phagspa, mastered that learning, and also understood the languages of the various peoples.

sentences.zh: 世祖闻其材，俾习中国之学，于是经、史、百家及阴阳、历数、图纬、方技之说皆通习之。

translations.literal: Kublai heard of his talents and had him study Chinese learning. Thereupon he thoroughly mastered the classics, histories, and the hundred schools, as well as the doctrines of yin-yang, calendrical reckoning, apocrypha and portents, and the various technical arts.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai heard of his abilities, he had him study the Chinese learning of the realm. Aluhunsali thereupon mastered the classics and histories, the teachings of the hundred schools, and the arts of yin-yang, calendrical reckoning, portents, and technical skill.

sentences.zh: 后事裕宗，入宿卫，深见器重。

translations.literal: Later he served Yuzong, entered the palace guard, and was deeply valued and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Yuzong, entered the palace guard, and won deep trust and esteem.

sentences.zh: 至元二十年，有西域僧自言能知天象，译者皆莫能通其说。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhiyuan, a monk from the Western Regions claimed he could read the heavenly signs, but none of the interpreters could follow his discourse.
translations.idiomatic: In 1283 a monk from the Western Regions claimed he could read the heavenly signs, yet none of the court interpreters could follow what he said.

sentences.zh: 帝问左右，谁可使者。

translations.literal: The emperor asked those around him who could be sent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his attendants whom he could send.

sentences.zh: 侍臣脱烈对曰：「阿鲁浑萨理可。」

translations.literal: Attendant Tolie replied: "Aluhunsali will do."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Tolie replied, "Aluhunsali will do."

sentences.zh: 即召与论难，僧大屈服。

translations.literal: He was immediately summoned to debate with him, and the monk was greatly humbled.
translations.idiomatic: Aluhunsali was summoned at once to debate with him, and the monk was thoroughly bested.

sentences.zh: 帝悦，令宿卫内朝。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and ordered him to serve in the palace guard at court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and ordered him to attend court audiences as a member of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 会有江南人言宋宗室反者，命遣使捕至阙下。

translations.literal: It happened that someone from Jiangnan reported that Song imperial clansmen were plotting rebellion; the emperor ordered envoys dispatched to seize them and bring them to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that someone from Jiangnan reported that members of the Song imperial clan were plotting rebellion, and the emperor ordered envoys sent to seize them and bring them to court.

sentences.zh: 使已发，阿鲁浑萨理趣入谏曰：「言者必妄，使不可遣。」

translations.literal: The envoys had already set out when Aluhunsali hastened in to remonstrate: "The accuser must be lying — the mission must not be sent."
translations.idiomatic: The envoys had already set out when Aluhunsali hurried in to remonstrate, "The accuser must be lying — the mission must not be sent."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿何以言之？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "On what grounds do you say this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "On what grounds do you say this?"

sentences.zh: 对曰：「若果反，郡县何以不知？

translations.literal: He replied: "If they had truly rebelled, how would the prefectures and counties not know?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If they had truly rebelled, how would the prefectures and counties not know?

sentences.zh: 言者不由郡县，而言之阙庭，必其仇也。

translations.literal: The accuser did not come through prefecture or county but brought word to the imperial court — he must be their enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The accuser did not come through prefecture or county but brought word straight to the imperial court — he must be their enemy.

sentences.zh: 且江南初定，民疑未附，一旦以小民浮言辄捕之，恐人人自危，徒中言者之计。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Jiangnan has only just been pacified and the people's allegiance is still uncertain. If on a commoner's idle word we at once seize people, I fear everyone will feel imperiled — and we would only play into the accuser's scheme."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Jiangnan has only just been pacified and the people's loyalty is still uncertain. If on a commoner's idle rumor we at once seize people, I fear everyone will feel imperiled — and we would only play into the accuser's scheme."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，立召使者还，俾械系言者下郡治之，言者立伏，果以尝贷钱不从诬之。

translations.literal: The emperor understood, immediately recalled the envoys, had the accuser shackled and sent down to the commandery for trial. The accuser promptly confessed — it turned out he had slandered them because they had once refused him a loan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood at once, recalled the envoys, had the accuser shackled and sent down to the local authorities for trial. The accuser promptly confessed — he had slandered them because they had once refused him a loan.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「非卿言，几误，但恨用卿晚耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "But for your words I would nearly have erred — only I regret employing you so late."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "But for your words I would nearly have erred — I only regret putting you to use so late."

sentences.zh: 自是命日侍左右。

translations.literal: From then on he was ordered to attend daily at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was ordered to attend daily at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，擢朝列大夫、左侍仪奉御。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to Court Rank Grandee and Left Attendant of Ceremonial Service.
translations.idiomatic: In 1284 he was promoted to Court Rank Grandee and left attendant of ceremonial service.

sentences.zh: 遂劝帝治天下必用儒术，宜招致山泽道艺之士，以备任使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he urged the emperor that to govern the realm one must employ Confucian methods, and that recluses and men of talent from mountains and marshes should be summoned to stand ready for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged the emperor that to govern the realm one must employ Confucian methods, and that recluses and men of talent from mountains and marshes should be summoned and kept ready for appointment.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉纳之，遣使求贤，置集贤馆以待之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this, dispatched envoys to seek the worthy, and established the Hall of Assembled Worthies to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted this counsel, dispatched envoys to seek out men of talent, and established the Hall of Assembled Worthies to receive them.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，命领馆事，阿鲁浑萨理曰：「陛下初置集贤以待士，宜择重望大臣领之，以新观听。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn he was ordered to direct the institute's affairs. Aluhunsali said: "Your Majesty first established the Hall of Assembled Worthies to await scholars — you should choose a great minister of heavy repute to head it, so as to refresh public regard."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn he was ordered to direct the institute's affairs. Aluhunsali said, "Your Majesty first established the Hall of Assembled Worthies to await scholars — you should choose a minister of great repute to head it, so as to refresh public regard."

sentences.zh: 请以司徒撒里蛮领其事，帝从之。

translations.literal: He requested that Minister of Works Sariman take charge of the matter, and the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Minister of Works Sariman take charge of the matter, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 仍以阿鲁浑萨理为中顺大夫、集贤馆学士，兼太史院事，仍兼左侍仪奉御。

translations.literal: Aluhunsali was then made Central Harmoniousness Grandee and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, concurrently serving in the Directorate of Astronomy, and still holding his post as Left Attendant of Ceremonial Service.
translations.idiomatic: Aluhunsali was then appointed Central Harmoniousness Grandee and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, concurrently serving in the Directorate of Astronomy while retaining his post as left attendant of ceremonial service.

sentences.zh: 士之应诏者，尽命馆谷之，凡饮食供帐，车服之盛，皆喜过望。

translations.literal: All scholars who answered the imperial summons were lodged and fed; in food, provisions, carriages, and raiment they were all delighted beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: All scholars who answered the imperial summons were lodged and fed at the hall; in food, provisions, carriages, and raiment they were all delighted beyond expectation.

sentences.zh: 其弗称旨者，亦请加赉而遣之。

translations.literal: Even those who did not meet the emperor's intent were additionally granted gifts and sent on their way.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who did not meet the emperor's expectations were additionally granted gifts and sent on their way.

sentences.zh: 有官于宣徽者，欲阴败其事，故盛陈所给廪饩于内前，冀帝见之。

translations.literal: An official of the Household Supply Directorate wished secretly to undermine the enterprise, so he lavishly displayed the rations provided before the inner palace, hoping the emperor would see them.
translations.idiomatic: An official of the Household Supply Directorate wished secretly to undermine the project, so he lavishly displayed the rations provided before the inner palace, hoping the emperor would see them.

sentences.zh: 帝果过而问焉，对曰：「此一士之日给也。」

translations.literal: The emperor indeed passed by and asked about it. [The official] replied: "This is one scholar's daily provision."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did pass by and asked about it. The official replied, "This is one scholar's daily provision."

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「汝欲使朕见而损之乎？

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Do you wish me to see this and cut it back?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said, "Do you wish me to see this and cut it back?

sentences.zh: 十倍此以待天下士，犹恐不至，况欲损之，谁肯至者。」

translations.literal: Ten times this to await the scholars of the realm — I still fear they will not come; how much less if you wish to reduce it — who would be willing to come?"
translations.idiomatic: Ten times this to receive the scholars of the realm — I still fear they will not come; how much less if you wish to reduce it — who would be willing to come?"

sentences.zh: 阿鲁浑萨理又言于帝曰：「国学人材之本，立国子监，置博士弟子员，宜优其廪饩，使学者日盛。」

translations.literal: Aluhunsali again spoke to the emperor: "The National University is the root of talent. Establishing the Directorate of Education with doctorate and student posts — their rations should be generously provided so that scholars daily increase."
translations.idiomatic: Aluhunsali spoke again to the emperor, "The National University is the root of talent. In establishing the Directorate of Education with doctorate and student posts, their rations should be generously provided so that scholars daily increase."

sentences.zh: 从之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 二十二年夏六月，迁嘉议大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer of the twenty-second year he was transferred to Distinguished Counsel Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer of 1285 he was transferred to Distinguished Counsel Grandee.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，进集贤大学士、中奉大夫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Central Submission Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In 1286 he was promoted to grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Central Submission Grandee.

sentences.zh: 二十四年春，立尚书省，桑哥用事，诏阿鲁浑萨理与同视事，固辞，不许，授资德大夫、尚书右丞，继拜荣禄大夫、平章政事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year the Ministry of Works was established; Sangge held power. An edict called Aluhunsali to join in administration of affairs. He firmly declined but was not permitted. He was granted Virtuous Virtue Grandee and Right Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works, then successively appointed Honorific Salary Grandee and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1287 the Ministry of Works was established and Sangge held power. An edict called Aluhunsali to join in the administration of affairs. He firmly declined but was not permitted. He was granted Virtuous Virtue Grandee and right vice minister of the Ministry of Works, then successively appointed Honorific Salary Grandee and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 桑哥为政暴横，且进其党与。

translations.literal: Sangge's governance was violent and overbearing, and he moreover advanced his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge governed with violence and overbearing arrogance, and he advanced his own faction.

sentences.zh: 阿鲁浑萨理数切诤之，久与乖剌，惟以廉正自持。

translations.literal: Aluhunsali repeatedly remonstrated sharply. Long estranged and at odds, he held to integrity and rectitude alone.
translations.idiomatic: Aluhunsali remonstrated with him sharply again and again. Long estranged and at odds, he held to integrity and rectitude alone.

sentences.zh: 桑哥奏立征理司，理天下逋欠，使者相望于道，所在囹圄皆满，道路侧目，无敢言者。

translations.literal: Sangge memorialized to establish the Tax Recovery Office to pursue arrears throughout the realm. Envoys filled the roads one after another; everywhere prisons were packed; travelers averted their eyes — none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge memorialized to establish the Tax Recovery Office to pursue tax arrears throughout the realm. Envoys filled the roads one after another, prisons everywhere were packed, travelers averted their eyes — and none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 会地震北京，阿鲁浑萨理请罢征理司，以塞天变。

translations.literal: When an earthquake struck Beiping, Aluhunsali requested abolishing the Tax Recovery Office to appease the heavenly portent.
translations.idiomatic: When an earthquake struck Beiping, Aluhunsali petitioned to abolish the Tax Recovery Office in order to appease the heavenly portent.

sentences.zh: 诏下之日，百姓相庆。

translations.literal: On the day the edict was issued, the people rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the edict was issued, the people rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 未几，桑哥败，以连坐，亦籍其产。

translations.literal: Before long Sangge fell. By implication of guilt, [Aluhunsali's] property was also confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sangge fell. By implication of guilt, Aluhunsali's property was also confiscated.

sentences.zh: 帝问：「桑哥为政如此，卿何故无一言？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Sangge governed thus — why did you not say a single word?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Sangge governed thus — why did you not say a single word?"

sentences.zh: 对曰：「臣未尝不言，顾言不用耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject never failed to speak — only my words were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your subject never failed to speak — only my words were not heeded.

sentences.zh: 陛下方信任桑哥甚，彼所忌独臣，臣数言不行，若抱柴救火，只益其暴，不若弥缝其间，使无伤国家大本，陛下久必自悟也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty was then trusting Sangge deeply. He hated none but me alone. My repeated words had no effect — like carrying faggots to put out fire, it would only increase his violence. Better to patch matters between them so as not to harm the state's great foundation; in time Your Majesty would surely awaken of yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was then trusting Sangge deeply. He hated none but me alone. My repeated remonstrances had no effect — like carrying faggots to put out a fire, they would only increase his violence. Better to patch matters between you so as not to harm the state's great foundation; in time Your Majesty would surely awaken of yourself."

sentences.zh: 帝亦以为然，且曰：「吾甚愧卿。」

translations.literal: The emperor also agreed, and moreover said: "I am very ashamed before you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also agreed, and added, "I am deeply ashamed before you."

sentences.zh: 桑哥临刑，吏犹以阿鲁浑萨理为问，桑哥曰：「我惟不用其言，故至于败，彼何与焉。」

translations.literal: At Sangge's execution the officials still questioned him about Aluhunsali. Sangge said: "It was only because I did not heed his words that I came to ruin — what has he to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: At Sangge's execution the officials still questioned him about Aluhunsali. Sangge said, "It was only because I did not heed his words that I came to ruin — what has he to do with it?"

sentences.zh: 帝益信其无罪，诏还所籍财产，仍遣张九思赐以金帛，辞不受。

translations.literal: The emperor believed all the more in his innocence, issued an edict returning his confiscated property, and still dispatched Zhang Jiusi to bestow gold and silk — he declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed all the more in his innocence, ordered his confiscated property returned, and dispatched Zhang Jiusi to bestow gold and silk — but Aluhunsali declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 二十八年秋，乞罢政事，并免太史院使，诏以为集贤大学士。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-eighth year he requested dismissal from administration, and also to be relieved of the directorship of the Directorate of Astronomy. An edict appointed him Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1291 he requested dismissal from administration and also to be relieved of the directorship of the Directorate of Astronomy. By edict he was appointed grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 司天刘监丞言，阿鲁浑萨理在太史院时，数言国家灾祥事，大不敬，请下吏治。

translations.literal: Astronomical Supervisor Liu reported that when Aluhunsali was at the Directorate of Astronomy he repeatedly spoke of the state's auspices and calamities — a great impropriety — and requested that he be handed over to the judicial officers.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomical Supervisor Liu reported that when Aluhunsali was at the Directorate of Astronomy he repeatedly spoke of the state's auspices and calamities — a grave impropriety — and requested that he be handed over to the judicial officers for punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，以为诽谤大臣，当抵罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry, deeming it slander of a great minister, fit for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered, deeming it slander of a great minister and fit for punishment.

sentences.zh: 阿鲁浑萨理顿首谢曰：「臣不佞，赖陛下天地含容之德，虽万死莫报。

translations.literal: Aluhunsali kowtowed and said: "Your subject is without talent, relying on Your Majesty's heaven-and-earth breadth of forbearance — though I should die ten thousand deaths I cannot repay it.
translations.idiomatic: Aluhunsali kowtowed and said, "Your subject is without talent, relying on Your Majesty's heaven-and-earth breadth of forbearance — though I should die ten thousand deaths I could not repay it.

sentences.zh: 然欲致言者罪，臣恐自是无为陛下言事者。」

translations.literal: Yet if you would punish the one who spoke, I fear from this there will be no one who speaks to Your Majesty on affairs of state."
translations.idiomatic: Yet if you would punish the one who spoke, I fear that from this there will be no one who speaks to Your Majesty on affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 力争之，乃得释。

translations.literal: He argued strenuously, and [the accuser] was released.
translations.idiomatic: He argued strenuously, and the accuser was released.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿真长者。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are truly an elder of worth."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are truly a man of noble character."

sentences.zh: 后虽罢政，或通夕召入论事，知无不言。

translations.literal: Later, though he had left office, sometimes he would be summoned through the night to discuss affairs — he spoke fully on all he knew.
translations.idiomatic: Later, though he had left office, sometimes he would be summoned through the night to discuss affairs, and he spoke fully on all he knew.

sentences.zh: 三十年，复领太史院事。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he again took charge of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1293 he again took charge of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝崩，成宗在边，裕宗太后命为书趣成宗入正大位，又命率翰林、集贤、礼官备礼册命。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor died. Chengzong was on the frontier. Empress Dowager of Yuzong ordered him to write urging Chengzong to enter and take the great throne, and also ordered him to lead Hanlin, Assembled Worthies, and rites officials to prepare the ceremonial patent of investiture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Kublai died. Chengzong was on the frontier. Yuzong's empress dowager ordered Aluhunsali to write urging Chengzong to enter and take the throne, and also ordered him to lead Hanlin, Assembled Worthies, and rites officials to prepare the ceremonial patent of investiture.

sentences.zh: 明年春，加守司徒、集贤院使，领太史院事。

translations.literal: The next spring he was additionally made Guardian Minister of Works and Director of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, continuing to head the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he was additionally made guardian minister of works and director of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, while continuing to head the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 初，裕宗即世，世祖欲定皇太子，未知所立，以问阿鲁浑萨理，即以成宗为封，且言成宗仁孝恭俭，宜立，于是大计乃决，成宗及裕宗皇后皆莫之知也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuzong passed away, Kublai wished to fix the Crown Prince but did not know whom to install. He asked Aluhunsali, who at once pointed to Chengzong and said Chengzong was filial, benevolent, reverent, and frugal — he should be installed. Thereupon the great decision was settled; Chengzong and Yuzong's empress knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yuzong died, Kublai wished to settle the succession but did not know whom to install. He asked Aluhunsali, who at once pointed to Chengzong and said that Chengzong was filial, benevolent, reverent, and frugal — he should be installed. Thereupon the great decision was settled; Chengzong and Yuzong's empress knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 数召阿鲁浑萨理不往，成宗抚军北边，帝遣阿鲁浑萨理奉皇太子宝于成宗，乃一至其邸。

translations.literal: Chengzong many times summoned Aluhunsali but he did not go. Chengzong held troops in the north; the emperor sent Aluhunsali to deliver the crown prince's seal to Chengzong — only then did he once visit his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong many times summoned Aluhunsali, but he did not go. Chengzong held troops in the north; the emperor sent Aluhunsali to deliver the crown prince's seal to Chengzong — only then did he visit his residence once.

sentences.zh: 及即位，语阿鲁浑萨理曰：「朕在潜邸，谁不愿事朕者，惟卿虽召不至，今乃知卿真得大臣体。」

translations.literal: When [Chengzong] took the throne he said to Aluhunsali: "When I was in my private estate, who did not wish to serve me? Only you, though summoned, did not come. Now I know you truly possess the bearing of a great minister."
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong took the throne he said to Aluhunsali, "When I was in my private estate, who did not wish to serve me? Only you, though summoned, did not come. Now I know you truly possess the bearing of a great minister."

sentences.zh: 自是召对不名，赐坐视诸侯王等。

translations.literal: From then on when summoned to audience his name was not called; he was granted a seat on a level with the feudal princes.
translations.idiomatic: From then on when summoned to audience his name was not called; he was granted a seat on a level with the feudal princes.

sentences.zh: 尝语左右曰：「若全平章者，真全材也，于今殆无其比。」

translations.literal: He once told those around him: "One like Grand Councillor Quan — truly a wholly complete talent; in our day there is scarcely his equal."
translations.idiomatic: He once told those around him, "A man like Grand Councillor Quan is truly a wholly complete talent — in our day there is scarcely his equal."

sentences.zh: 大德三年，复拜中书平章政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade he was again appointed Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1299 he was again appointed grand councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，薨，年六十有三。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1307, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 延祐四年，赠推忠佐理翊亮功臣、太师、开府仪同三司、上柱国，追封赵国公，谥文定。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanyou he was posthumously given the title Meritorious Minister for Supporting Loyalty, Assisting Governance, and Illuminating Brightness, Grand Preceptor, with carriage, seal, and Three Excellencies of a feudatory opening establishment, Senior Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: In 1317 he was posthumously given the title Meritorious Minister for Supporting Loyalty, Assisting Governance, and Illuminating Brightness, grand preceptor, with carriage, seal, and Three Excellencies of a feudatory opening establishment, and senior pillar of state; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with the posthumous title Cultured and Settled.

sentences.zh: 子三人：长岳柱；

translations.literal: He had three sons: the eldest Yuezhu;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons. The eldest was Yuezhu;

sentences.zh: 次久著，终翰林侍读学士；

translations.literal: the second Jiuzhu, who ended as Hanlin Associate Reader;
translations.idiomatic: the second, Jiuzhu, who ended as Hanlin associate reader;

sentences.zh: 次买住，蚤卒。

translations.literal: the third Maizhu, who died young.
translations.idiomatic: the third, Maizhu, who died young.

sentences.zh: 岳柱自有传。

translations.literal: Yuezhu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhu has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 阿台萨理赠保德功臣、银青荣禄大夫、司徒、柱国，追封赵国公，谥端愿；

translations.literal: Atai Sali was posthumously given Meritorious Minister for Preserving Virtue, Silver-Green Honorific Salary Grandee, Minister of Works, Pillar of State, posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Zhao with posthumous title Duanyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Atai Sali was posthumously given the title Meritorious Minister for Preserving Virtue, Silver-Green Honorific Salary Grandee, minister of works, and pillar of state; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with the posthumous title Upright and Sincere;

sentences.zh: 乞台萨理累赠纯诚守正功臣、太保、仪同三司、上柱国，追封赵国公，谥通敏。

translations.literal: Qitai Sali was cumulatively posthumously given Meritorious Minister of Pure Sincerity and Upright Guarding, Grand Guardian, with carriage and seal and Three Excellencies, Senior Pillar of State, posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Zhao with posthumous title Tongmin.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai Sali was cumulatively posthumously given the title Meritorious Minister of Pure Sincerity and Upright Guarding, grand guardian, with carriage and seal and Three Excellencies, and senior pillar of state; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with the posthumous title Comprehensive and Keen.

sentences.zh: 岳柱字止所，一字兼山。

translations.literal: Yuezhu, courtesy name Zhisuo, also styled Jianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhu, courtesy name Zhisuo, also styled Jianshan.

sentences.zh: 自幼容止端严，性颖悟，有远识。

translations.literal: From youth his bearing was dignified and decorous; by nature he was quick-witted and far-sighted.
translations.idiomatic: From youth his bearing was dignified and decorous; by nature he was quick-witted and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 方八岁，观画师何澄画《陶母剪发图》，岳柱指陶母手中金钏诘之曰：「金钏可易酒，何用剪发为也？」

translations.literal: At just eight years old, viewing the painter He Cheng's "Lady Tao Shearing Her Hair," Yuezhu pointed at the golden bracelet in Lady Tao's hand and questioned: "The bracelet could be exchanged for wine — what need to shear hair?"
translations.idiomatic: At just eight years old, viewing the painter He Cheng's Lady Tao Shearing Her Hair, Yuezhu pointed at the golden bracelet in Lady Tao's hand and asked, "The bracelet could be exchanged for wine — why shear hair instead?"

sentences.zh: 何大惊，即异之。

translations.literal: He was greatly startled and at once regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He Cheng was greatly startled and at once regarded the boy as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 既长就学，日记千言。

translations.literal: When grown he entered upon study and daily wrote a thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew older and entered upon his studies, he wrote a thousand words each day.

sentences.zh: 年十八，从丞相答失蛮备宿卫，出入禁中，如老成人。

translations.literal: At eighteen he followed Chancellor Dashman in palace guard duty, entering and leaving the inner palace like a seasoned elder.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he followed Chancellor Dashman in palace guard duty, entering and leaving the inner palace with the bearing of a seasoned elder.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，授集贤学士，阶正议大夫，即以荐贤举能为事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was appointed Academician of Assembled Worthies at the rank of Righteousness Discussion Grandee, and at once took recommending the worthy and advancing the capable as his business.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he was appointed academician of Assembled Worthies at the rank of Righteousness Discussion Grandee, and at once took recommending the worthy and advancing the capable as his business.

sentences.zh: 皇庆元年，升中奉大夫、湖南道宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was promoted to Central Submission Grandee and Pacification Commissioner of Hunan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1312 he was promoted to Central Submission Grandee and pacification commissioner of Hunan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 日接见儒生，询求民瘼。

translations.literal: Daily he received Confucian scholars and inquired into the people's grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he received Confucian scholars and inquired into the people's grievances.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，进资善大夫、隆禧院使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou he was promoted to Nurture-the-Good Grandee and Director of the Directorate of Imperial Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: In 1316 he was promoted to Nurture-the-Good Grandee and director of the Directorate of Imperial Blessings.

sentences.zh: 七年，授太史院使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1320 he was appointed director of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 英宗视其进止整暇，顾谓参政速速曰：「全院使真故家令子也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong observed his composed and unhurried demeanor, turned and said to Vice Administrator Susu: "Director Quan is truly a noble scion of an old family."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong observed his composed and unhurried demeanor, turned and said to Vice Administrator Susu, "Director Quan is truly a noble scion of an old family."

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，改太常礼仪院使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was transferred to Director of the Directorate of Imperial Rites and Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1324 he was transferred to director of the Directorate of Imperial Rites and Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 四年，授礼部尚书，领会同馆事，俄授江西等处行中书省参知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Minister of Rites, concurrently directing the Hall of Mutual Association, and shortly thereafter made Vice Administrator of the Branch Secretariat of Jiangxi and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In 1327 he was appointed minister of rites and placed in charge of the Hall of Mutual Association, and shortly thereafter made vice administrator of the Branch Secretariat of Jiangxi and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 天历元年，进荣禄大夫、集贤大学士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli he was promoted to Honorific Salary Grandee and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1328 he was promoted to Honorific Salary Grandee and grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 至顺二年，除江西等处行中书省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Jiangxi and other circuits Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhishun (1331) he was appointed pacification commissioner of the Jiangxi regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 时有诬告富民负永宁王官帑钱八百餘锭者，中书遣使诸路征之。

translations.literal: At the time there were false accusations that wealthy households owed more than eight hundred ingots of the Prince of Yongning's official treasury funds; the Central Secretariat sent envoys to all circuits to collect them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time false accusations claimed that wealthy households owed more than eight hundred ingots from the Prince of Yongning's official treasury. The Central Secretariat sent envoys to all circuits to collect the sums.

sentences.zh: 使至江西，岳柱曰：「事涉诬罔，不可奉命。」

translations.literal: When the envoy reached Jiangxi, Yuezhu said, "The matter involves false accusation — I cannot obey the order."
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy reached Jiangxi, Yuezhu said, "The matter involves false accusation. I cannot obey this order."

sentences.zh: 僚佐重违宰臣意，岳柱曰：「民惟邦本，伤本以敛怨，亦非宰相福也。」

translations.literal: His subordinates feared going against the chief ministers' intent; Yuezhu said, "The people are the foundation of the state — to wound the foundation to gather resentment is no blessing for a chancellor either."
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates feared defying the chief ministers. Yuezhu said, "The people are the foundation of the state. To wound that foundation and gather resentment is no blessing for a chancellor either."

sentences.zh: 令使者以此意复命。

translations.literal: He had the envoy return and report in these terms.
translations.idiomatic: He had the envoy return and report in these terms.

sentences.zh: 时燕帖木兒为丞相，闻其言，感悟，命刑部诘治，得诬罔状，罪诬告者若干人。

translations.literal: At the time El Temür was chief minister; hearing Yuezhu's words he was moved to understanding and ordered the Ministry of Punishments to investigate; the false accusation was established and several accusers were punished.
translations.idiomatic: El Temür was then chief minister. Hearing Yuezhu's words, he was moved and ordered the Ministry of Punishments to investigate. The false accusation was proved, and several accusers were punished.

sentences.zh: 宰相以奏，帝嘉之，特赐币帛及上尊酒。

translations.literal: The chief minister reported this; the emperor commended him and specially granted silks and fine wine of the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister reported this to the throne. The emperor commended Yuezhu and specially granted him silks and wine of the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 桂阳州民张思进等，啸聚二千餘众，州县不能治，广东宣慰司请发兵捕之。

translations.literal: Zhang Sijin and others of Guiyang Prefecture gathered more than two thousand followers in a band; the prefecture and county could not control them, and the Guangdong Pacification Commission requested troops to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sijin and others of Guiyang Prefecture gathered more than two thousand followers in a band. The prefecture and county could not control them, and the Guangdong pacification commission requested troops to capture them.

sentences.zh: 岳柱曰：「有司不能抚绥边民，乃欲侥幸兴兵，以为民害耶？

translations.literal: Yuezhu said, "The officials cannot pacify and comfort the border people, yet wish by luck to raise troops and bring harm to the people?
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhu said, "The officials cannot pacify the border people, yet hope by luck to raise troops and bring harm to the people?

sentences.zh: 不可。」

translations.literal: This cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: That cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 宰执皆失色，宪司亦以兴兵不便为言，岳柱终持不可，遣千户王英往问状。

translations.literal: The chief ministers all changed color; the censorate also said raising troops was inadvisable; Yuezhu held firm that it could not be done and sent the chiliarch Wang Ying to inquire into the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers all paled. The censorate also said raising troops was inadvisable. Yuezhu held firm and sent the chiliarch Wang Ying to inquire into the facts.

sentences.zh: 英直抵贼巢，谕以祸福，贼曰：「致我为非者，两巡检司耳，我等何敢有异心哉！」

translations.literal: Wang Ying went straight to the bandits' lair and lectured them on fortune and disaster; the bandits said, "Those who drove us to wrongdoing were only the two patrol offices — how would we dare harbor divergent hearts!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying went straight to the bandits' lair and lectured them on fortune and disaster. The bandits said, "Only the two patrol offices drove us to this — how would we dare harbor rebellious hearts!"

sentences.zh: 谕其众，皆使复业，一方以宁。

translations.literal: He lectured their followers, and all were made to return to their occupations; the region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured their followers, and all were made to return to their occupations. The region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 三年，迁河南江北等处行中书省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the Henan and Jiangbei circuits Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1332) he was transferred to pacification commissioner of the Henan and Jiangbei regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 旋以军事至扬州，得疾，明年十二月，端坐而卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on military business he reached Yangzhou, fell ill, and in the twelfth month of the following year died sitting upright, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on military business he reached Yangzhou and fell ill. In the twelfth month of the following year he died sitting upright, aged fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 岳柱天资孝友，母弟久住早卒，丧之尽哀。

translations.literal: Yuezhu was filial and fraternal by nature; his younger brother by the same mother, Jiuzhu, died early, and he mourned him with the utmost grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhu was filial and fraternal by nature. His younger brother by the same mother, Jiuzhu, died young, and he mourned him with the utmost grief.

sentences.zh: 尤嗜经史，自天文、医药之书，无不究极。

translations.literal: He was especially fond of the classics and histories; from books on astronomy and medicine, none escaped his thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially fond of the classics and histories. From astronomy to medicine, no book escaped his thorough study.

sentences.zh: 度量弘扩，有欺之者，恬不为意。

translations.literal: His breadth of mind was great; when others deceived him, he was calmly unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: His breadth of mind was great. When others deceived him, he remained calmly unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 或问之，则曰：「彼自欺也，我何与焉。」

translations.literal: When asked about it, he would say, "They deceive themselves — what has it to do with me?"
translations.idiomatic: When asked about it, he would say, "They deceive themselves. What has that to do with me?"

sentences.zh: 母郜氏亦常称之曰：「吾子古人也。」

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Gao, also often said of him, "My son is a man of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Gao, also often said of him, "My son is a man of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 子四人：长普达，同佥行宣政院事；

translations.literal: He had four sons: the eldest, Puda, served as Associate Commissioner of the Regional Commission for Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: the eldest, Puda, served as associate commissioner of the regional commission for Buddhist and Tibetan affairs;

sentences.zh: 次安僧，为久住后，章佩监丞；

translations.literal: the second, Anseng, was posthumous heir to Jiuzhu and Supervisor of the Directorate of Insignia;
translations.idiomatic: the second, Anseng, was posthumous heir to Jiuzhu and supervisor of the Directorate of Insignia;

sentences.zh: 次仁寿，中宪大夫、长秋寺卿。

translations.literal: the third, Renshou, was Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Director of the Directorate of the Autumn Palace.
translations.idiomatic: the third, Renshou, was grand master of palace attendance and director of the Directorate of the Autumn Palace.
